q: One characteristic of a deliberative assembly is that the size of the group is usually less than six.*
exp: The size of the group in a deliberative assembly when a degree of formality is desired, is uSually over a dozen.

q: A member who does not agree with a decision made by a deliberative assembly should be asked by the president to withdraw from the society before the next regular meeting.
exp: A member who does not agree with a decision made by a deliberative assembly is not withdrawn from the society.

q: The questions acted upon in a deliberative assembly are normally decided by the members who are present at a regular meeting.
An assembly is a series of meetings.
exp: An assembly is a body of people who come together as a group. A session is one or more connected meetings (a series of meetings).

q: A member of an assembly is a person having the right to participate fully in its proceedings.
Members of a deliberative assembly may make motions, participate in debate, and vote.
A deliberative assembly that has not adopted rules to govern its organization is bound by the rules and customs of the constitution of its State.
exp: A deliberative assembly that has not adopted rules to govem its organization is bound by the rules and customs of common parliamentary aw.

q: The actions of any deliberative assembly are subject to the bylaws and other rules of its organization and all applicable ocal, state, and national laws.
The basic principle of decision in a deliberative assembly is that a two-thirds vote is required for the adoption of all propositions.
exp: The basic principle of decision in a deliberative assembly is that propositions are adopted by a majority vote.

q: In a deliberative assembly, a proposition may be adopted by a majority vote, which means that a motion must be approved by more than half of the members present and voting.
When an organization needs to make a decision that requires more than a majority vote, common requirements are a two-thirds vote and possibly previous notice.
If previous notice is not announced at the preceding meeting, the notice of the proposal to be brought up must be ncluded in the "call" of the meeting at which it is to be taken up.
The call of a meeting is a verbal notice of a future meeting.
exp: The calf of a meeting is a written notice of the time and place of the meeting which is mailed or distributed to members.

q: A committee is a principal type of deliberative assembly.
exp: A committee is not a principal type of a deliberative assembly. Mass meetings, legislative bodies, the assembly of organized societies, conventions, and boards are the principal types of deliberative assemblies.

q: When an unorganized group meets to discuss a specific problem and anyone may attend who is interested, it is called a mass meeting.
Admittance to a mass meeting may be limited.
exp: A mass meeting may be limited to those who are interested in the purpose of the meeting.

q: Only the elected officers and the parliamentarian have the right to participate at a mass meeting.
exp: Everyone who supports the purpose of the meeting has the right to attend and participate at a mass meeting.

q: A mass meeting does not need a large attendance to function.Page numbers refer to the 2000 edition of Robert's Rules of Order Newly Revised.
Most people will ordinarily have some experience in a deliberative assembly such as a local branch of an organized permanent society.
exp: An example would be a local club and a school board.

q: The bylaws of an organized local society usually provide that it shall hold special meetings every month.
exp: The bylaws of an organized local society usually provide that it shall hold regular meetings at stated intervals.

q: Organized local societies are characterized by having each meeting normally serve as a separate session.
An assembly of delegates normally chosen for one session is called a "delegation."
exp: An assembly of delegates normally chosen for one session is called a "convention."

q: The voting membership of a convention usually consists of delegates.
When a convention concludes, alternate delegates begin their own "Alternate Convention."
exp: When a convention concludes, the assembly is normally dissolved.

q: Law-making groups such as Congress are called "mass meetings."
exp: Law-making groups such as Congress are called "legislative bodies."

q: Legislative bodies such as a state legislature usually consist of one group and its sessions may continue up to one month.
exp: Legislative bodies such as a state legislature usually consist of two "houses" and its sessions may continue for months.

q: A board is an administrative body that must be appointed.
exp: A board is an administrative body that is elected or appointed.

q: A board generally has many of the same character of a deliberative assembly.
The minimum size of a board is 4.
exp: Boards have no minimum size and are usually smaller than assemblies.

q: A board within an organized society has responsibilities that are conferred on it by authority outside itself.
Large boards and large committees follow parliamentary procedure when the presiding officer determines it will benefit the meeting.
exp: Large boards and large committees usually follow parliamentary procedure in the same way as any assembly.

q: Certain rules are established by an organized society to determine its basic structure and manner of operation.
section: 2. Rules Of An Assembly Or Organization
exp: Examples are bylaws and rules of order as designated by a parliamentary authority.

q: The Corporate Charter of a society that wishes to be incorporated should contain the name of the society, the object of the society, and any information required of the particular state where the society originated.
section: 2. Rules Of An Assembly Or Organization

q: One principal advantage of incorporating a society is that the officers and members can change the bylaws without a vote of the members.
section: 2. Rules Of An Assembly Or Organization
exp: One advantage of incorporating a society is that the members are protected from personal liability under obligations when they act on behalf of the organization that may be incurred by the organization.

q: A corporate charter should be drafted by the first officers of an organization.
section: 2. Rules Of An Assembly Or Organization
exp: A corporate charter should be drafted by an attomey.

q: In an incorporated organization, the document that supersedes all other rules is the constitution.
section: 2. Rules Of An Assembly Or Organization
exp: In an incorporated organization, the document that supersedes all other rules is the charter.

q: The document of a society that contains its own rules relating to itself as an organization is the constitution or bylaws.
section: 2. Rules Of An Assembly Or Organization

q: The usual term used in Robert's Rules of Order Newly Revised that refers to a combination of the bylaws and constitution is Statutes.
section: 2. Rules Of An Assembly Or Organization
exp: The usual term used in Robert's Rules of Order Newly Revised that refers to a combination of the bylaws and constitution is bylaws.

q: Generally, the bylaws of an organization include the principal characteristics of the organization, how the organization ; unctions, and the rules that the organization believes are important.
section: 2. Rules Of An Assembly Or Organization

q: A mnemonic commonly used to remember the articles of bylaws is "NO MOME C PA" (Say, "No Mommy, see Pa.") The two "M's" represent Members and Meetings.
section: 2. Rules Of An Assembly Or Organization

q: The first two articles in the bylaws of an unincorporated society are Name of Officers and Duties.
section: 2. Rules Of An Assembly Or Organization
exp: The first two articles in the bylaws of an unincorporated society are The Name of the Organization and its Object.

q: An article listing all the members' legal names and addresses is not included in an organization's bylaws.
section: 2. Rules Of An Assembly Or Organization

q: In an incorporated society, the articles that are generally not included in bylaws are the Name and Members.
section: 2. Rules Of An Assembly Or Organization
exp: In an incorporated society, the articles that are generally not included in bylaws are the Name and Object.

q: An incorporated society should not have the constitution separated from the bylaws.
section: 2. Rules Of An Assembly Or Organization

q: Except for the corporate charter in an incorporated society, the highest body of rules are the standing rules.J
section: 2. Rules Of An Assembly Or Organization
exp: Except for the corporate charter in an incorporated society, bylaws are the highest body of rules.

q: If an organization has both a constitution and bylaws as separate documents, the constitution is higher ruling.
section: 2. Rules Of An Assembly Or Organization

q: The written rules of parliamentary procedure formally adopted by an assembly or an organization are known as the rules of order.
section: 2. Rules Of An Assembly Or Organization

q: The term rules of order refers to the adopted bylaws.
section: 2. Rules Of An Assembly Or Organization
exp: The term rules of order refers to the rules of parliamentary procedure that an organization must use.

q: Ordinary societies usually provide themselves with rules of order by naming an edition of a parliamentary law manual n its bylaws. This manual is then called the organization's parliamentary authority.
section: 2. Rules Of An Assembly Or Organization
exp: Robert's Rules of Order Newly Revised is used as a parliamentary authority by many organizations. ;

q: Rules of order that supplement or modify the rules contained in an organization's parliamentary authority are called the secondary parliamentary authority.
section: 2. Rules Of An Assembly Or Organization
exp: Rules of order that supplement or modify the rules contained in an organization's parliamentary authority are called ial rules of order.

q: Ina mass meeting or a meeting of a body not yet organized, a parliamentary authority may be adopted at the beginning of the meeting.
section: 2. Rules Of An Assembly Or Organization

q: If a special rule of order is not in agreement with an organization's parliamentary authority, the parliamentary authority must be used.
section: 2. Rules Of An Assembly Or Organization
exp: Ifa special rule of order is not in agreement with an organization's parliamentary authority, the special rule of order must be used.

q: If an organization has adopted Robert's Rules of Order Newly Revised as their parliamentary authority and another manual disagrees with a specific rule, Robert's Rules of Order Newly Revised is binding.
section: 2. Rules Of An Assembly Or Organization

q: Special rules of order should be adopted as part of the bylaws.
section: 2. Rules Of An Assembly Or Organization
exp: Special rules of order should be adopted separately from the bylaws.

q: Special rules of order should be listed in the same booklet as the bylaws, but under a separate heading.
section: 2. Rules Of An Assembly Or Organization

q: The minimum affirmative vote necessary to suspend rules of order named in an organization's parliamentary authority or adopted as special rules of order is two-thirds of the members present and voting.
section: 2. Rules Of An Assembly Or Organization

q: The minimum affirmative vote necessary to adopt or amend special rules of order that are separate from the bylaws s a majority of those present.
section: 2. Rules Of An Assembly Or Organization
exp: The minimum affirmative vote necessary to adopt or amend special rules of order that are separate from the bylaws is two-thirds with previous notice, or a vote of a majority of the entire membership.

q: Standing rules are associated with the particulars of administration and not parliamentary procedure.
section: 2. Rules Of An Assembly Or Organization

q: Ordinary standing rules generally contain an hour that sets the time meetings are to begin.
section: 2. Rules Of An Assembly Or Organization

q: An example of a standing rule is defining a quorum for the organization.
section: 2. Rules Of An Assembly Or Organization
exp: An example of a standing rule is the maintenance of a guest register. The quorum is defined in the bylaws or parliamentary authority.

q: Standing rules for an organization are usually adopted before the society is organized.
section: 2. Rules Of An Assembly Or Organization
exp: Standing rules for an organization are usually adopted after the society is organized and the bylaws are adopted.

q: The minimum affirmative vote to adopt a standing rule at any business meeting is two-thirds without previous notice.
section: 2. Rules Of An Assembly Or Organization
exp: The minimum affirmative vote to adopt a standing rule at any business meeting is a majority without previous notice.

q: A standing rule remains in effect until the end of the meeting.
section: 2. Rules Of An Assembly Or Organization
exp: A standing rule remains in effect until rescinded or amended.

q: At a formal meeting, and without notice, a deliberative assembly has the right to temporarily suspend its standing rules.P 11
section: 2. Rules Of An Assembly Or Organization

q: The quorum of an assembly is the number of members who always vote on motions brought before the assembly.
exp: The quorum of an assembly is the number of members who must be present at a meeting for business to be legally transacted.

q: In both houses of the Congress of the United States, the quorum is a majority of the members.
In the absence of a provision in the bylaws, the quorum of an organized society is a majority of the entire membership.
The minimum essential officers that must be present to conduct business in a deliberative assembly are a president and vice-president.
exp: The minimum essential officers that must be present to conduct business in a deliberative assembly are a presiding officer and a secretary or clerk.

q: If an organization's officers are members of the assembly, they are counted when deciding if a quorum is present.
The phrase "the chairman" refers both to the presiding officer and to the station in the place where he/she presides.
exp: The phrase "the chair' refers both to the presiding officer and to the station in the place where he/she presides.

q: The presiding officer at a meeting is usually addressed as "Mr. or Madam Presiding Officer."
exp: The presiding officer at a meeting is usually addressed as "Mr. or Madam President" or "Mr. or Madam Chairman."

q: The president of a club who is a married or unmarried woman should be addressed as "Mrs. President."
exp: The president of a club who is a married or unmarried woman should be addressed as "Madam President."

q: The vice-president should be addressed as "Mr. or Madam President" while actually presiding if the president is not on the platform.
With very few exceptions (such as small boards and committees), a member never speaks while seated.
During a regular meeting, the presiding officer refers to himself/herself as "I."
exp: During a regular meeting, the presiding officer refers to himself/herself in the third person as "the Chair."

q: The chair should not mention a member's name except when calling him/her out of order.
exp: The chair may mention a member's name when assigning the floor, announcing committee members, or naming a committee chair.

q: An appropriate phrase to use by the presiding officer to call a meeting to order is "The meeting will come to order."
The order of business stipulates the sequence in which certain general types or classes of business are brought up or permitted to be offered at a meeting.
The order of business outline in Robert's Rules of Order Newly Revised must be followed if a society has adopted it or its parliamentary authority.
exp: A society which has adopted Robert's Rules of Order Newly Revised as its parliamentary authority may adopt its own particular order of business.

q: After the presiding officer calls a meeting to order, the next order of business is usually reading and approval of the minutes.
In the order of business, reports of Special Committees should immediately follow the reports of Officers, Boards, and Standing Committees.
In the standard order of business, the reports of officers are presented only as time allows.
exp: In the standard order of business, the reports of officers are presented immediately after approval of the minutes.

q: In the standard order of business, New Business immediately follows Special Orders.
exp: In the standard order of business, Unfinished Business immediately follows Special Orders.

q: In the standard order of business, New Business is taken up after Unfinished Business and General Orders.
A mass meeting usually does not need an order of business because unfinished business is taken up first.
exp: A mass meeting usually does not need an order of business because only new business can be brought up.

q: A convention ordinarily adopts its own order of business.
Calling a meeting to order is not part of the order of business.
The order of business of a convention is designated as the agenda or the program.
Business is brought before an assembly by a member making a formal proposai called an order.
exp: Business is brought before an assembly by a member making a formal proposal called a motion.

q: The only motion whose introduction brings business before an assembly is a primary amendment.
exp: The only motion whose introduction brings business before an assembly is a main motion.

q: A communication addressed to the organization is normally read aloud at a meeting by the president.
exp: A communication addressed to the organization is normaily read aloud at a meeting by the secretary.

q: The reading of a communication at a meeting means that a motion is not formally before the assembly.
The formal parliamentary name given to any form of discussion of the merits of a motion is called an argument.
exp: The formal parliamentary name given to any form of discussion of the merits of a motion is called debate.

q: Any member who seeks the floor while entitled to it must be recognized by the chair.a 33. Before members in a large assembly can debate or propose motions, they first must address the chair.

Before a member of an assembly is allowed to speak or propose a motion, he or she must obiain the floor. This means that the member must rise, address the chair, and wait to be recognized before speaking.
if the presiding officer believes a member is entitled to the floor, the member is recognized by the chair announcing the member's name, title, or the unit that he/she represents.
When a member "has the floor," this means that recognition has been received from the chair.
A member addressing the chair to claim the floor when the names of the members are not known should wait until the presiding officer asks his/her name.
exp: Amember addressing the chair to claim the floor when the names of the members are not known should state his/her name and appropriate dentifying information.

q: When a member yields the floor by sitting, this means that there is an immediate vote on the pending motion.
exp: When a member yields the floor by sitting, this means that the member is finished speaking.

q: The expression "privileges of the floor" means that a person is permitted to enter the room in which a meeting is being held.
Generally, if two members rise at about the same time, the chair should recognize the member who raised a hand and stood up.
exp: Generally, if two members rise at about the same time, the chair should recognize the member who rose and addressed the chair first after the floor was yielded. Members do not need to raise a hand to be recognized.

q: If you were the presiding officer and several members addressed the chair at about the same time after a motion was made, you should call on the member who made the motion and has not debated.
During the debate of a motion, the chair should alternate between the maker of the motion and members who oppose t.
exp: During the debate of a motion, the chair should alternate between members who want to speak pro (favoring) and con (opposing)

q: If the chair makes a mistake and assigns the floor to the wrong member, attention to correct the error can be called by a member immediately raising a Point of Order.

A Point of Order may be raised if the chair overlooks the fact that the rules of the assembly are being violated, or does not rule a main motion out of order that is outside the objectives of the society.
A motion is brought before the assembly by a member making a motion and the chair stating it.F
exp: A motion is brought before the assembly by a member making a motion, another member seconding it, and the chair stating it.

q: The words move, make, and offer refer to the first step by which a motion is brought before an assembly.
After a motion is made and seconded, the member who made the motion debates it and this places it before the assembly.
exp: After a motion is made and seconded, it is placed before the assembly by the chair Stating the question.

q: After a motion is made, seconded, and restated by the chair, the motion is pending.
If an assembly decides to do what a motion proposes, the motion is endorsed.
exp: If an assembly decides to do what a motion proposes, the motion is carried or adopted.

q: If an assembly decides not to do what a motion proposes, the motion is rejected or lost.
Main motions should start with the words "I motion that . . ."
exp: Main motions should start with the words "Il move that..."

q: Complex motions are presented in the form of a resolution.
Because resolutions are long and complicated, they should be put into writing before being presented and given to the chair after being offered to the assembly.
The member who proposes a main motion has the right to debate it last.
exp: The member who proposes a main motion has the right to speak in debate first.

q: A member should debate a motion immediately after it is made.
exp: Immediately after members make motions, they should resume their seats.

q: If a member did not hear a motion that was made at a meeting, it can be repeated by the chair, secretary, or the maker of the motion.
Before proposing a main motion, a member may explain all reasons in detail for making the motion.
exp: Before proposing a main motion, a member may offer an explanation of a few words. It cannot become a speech.

q: Members who are unsure of the proper wording of a motion may seek assistance from the chair.
In large assemblies, a member must second a motion before it may be considered.
The seconder of a motion must be recognized by the chair.
exp: The seconder of a motion does not need to obtain the floor or raise a hand.

q: After a main motion has been made, another member--without obtaining the floor and who wishes the motion to be considered--says "I second the motion," "I second it," or "Second."
In large assemblies, a motion should be seconded by a member saying, "I second it," without obtaining the floor.
exp: In large assemblies, a motion should be seconded by a member standing, stating hisher name without being recognized, and saying, Mr./Madam President, I second the motion."

q: In some organizations, instead of using the word "second" to indicate that a motion shall be considered, members use the word "subscribe."
exp: In some organizations, instead of using the word "second" to indicate that a motion shall be considered, members use the word "support."

q: Assume you are the chair at a large meeting. If a member makes a motion, but it is not seconded immediately, you should repeat the motion and ask, "Is there a second to the motion?"
Motions proposed in small boards or committees must be seconded.
exp: Motions proposed in small boards or committees need not be seconded.

q: If a main motion is not seconded, the chair would say, "Since there is no second, will the maker of the motion withdraw t?"
exp: If a main motion is not seconded, the chair would say, "Since there is no second, the motion is not before this meeting."

q: After notifying the assembly that a motion has not been seconded, the chair says, "The next item of business s..."
A second suggests that the seconder agrees that the motion should be adopted without change.
exp: A second suggests that the seconder agrees that the motion should come before the assembly.

q: A member who is opposed to a motion may second it.
Committee motions require a second if the committee consists of over two persons. ( Page 35)
exp: Committee motions require a second only if the committee consists of one person.

q: The requirement of a second to a motion is for the guidance of the chair so that the question on the motion can be stated.
The purpose of a second to a motion is to stop time from being used up by the assembly having to dispose of a motion that only a single member wishes to be introduced.
If the chair is sure that over a majority of the assembly approves a motion, a second must still be made.
exp: if the chair is sure that over a majority of the assembly approves a motion, the question can be stated without a second.

q: If a controversial motion was not seconded before it was stated by the chair, any member should raise a call for the orders of the day.
exp: Ifa controversial motion was not seconded before it was stated by the chair, any member should raise a point of order.

q: If a motion is considered and adopted without having been seconded, it is lost.
exp: If a motion is considered and adopted without having been seconded, it is still adopted.

q: After a motion is made and seconded, the chair states the question. This means that the chair repeats the exact motion and indicates it is open for debate.
A debatable motion is placed on the floor and is opened for debate after the motion has been seconded.
exp: A debatable motion is placed on the floor and is opened for debate after the motion has been stated by the chair.

q: The statement by the chair, "Are you ready for the question?" means the members may debate the pending question.
A proper statement by the chair after a motion has been made and seconded is, "It is moved and seconded that..."
If a motion is made that cannot be debated or amended, the chair would put the motion to a vote immediately after stating it.
exp: When the chair puts the motion, this means it is put to a vote.

q: Usually the chair must state the question on a motion immediately after it is made.
exp: Usually the chair must state the question on a motion immediately after it is made and seconded.

q: When a member's motion is not in order, the chair says, "You are out of order because . . ."
exp: When a member's motion is not in order, the chair says, "The chair rules that the motion is out of order because . . ."

q: The wording of a motion may be changed and recorded in the minutes by the secretary after the meeting.
exp: A motion is recorded in the minutes as it was stated by the chair just before being voted on by the assembly.

q: Before a main motion is stated to the assembly, the chair can require that it be in writing
exp: The chair can also require an amendment be in writing before he/she states it.

q: The maker of a motion has the right to modify or withdraw it until the chair states the question.
Debate is not in order after a main motion has been made and before it is stated by the chair.
The seconder of a motion has the right to withdraw his/her second if the maker of the motion modifies the motion that was seconded before it is stated by the chair.
The proper order of steps in considering a main motion are the chair puts the question, the chair announces the results of the voting, and members debate.
exp: The proper order of steps in considering a main motion are members debate, the chair puts the question, and the chair announces the voting results.

q: Immediately after stating the question, the chair should turn toward the maker of the motion to see if he/she wants the assembly to vote immediately without debate.
exp: Immediately after stating the question, the chair should tum toward the maker of the motion to see if he or she wishes to be assigned the oor to debate.

q: The maker of a motion must always speak first in debate on the motion.
exp: The maker of a motion has the fight to speak first in debate on the motion. ‘ ‘

q: Unless there is a rule to the contrary, a member may speak three times on the same motion on the same day.
exp: Unless there is a rule to the contrary, a member may speak twice on the same motion on the same day.

q: When a member has exhausted his/her right to debate a particular motion for that day, it means that the member has debated the motion twice and cannot make a third speech related to it on the same day.
A member may speak two minutes each time on a pending motion unless permission is given by the assembly or it s outlined differently in the bylaws.
exp: A member may speak ten minutes each time on a pending motion unless permission is given by the assembly or it is outlined differently n the bylaws.

q: Debate on a motion must be confined to the merits of the immediately pending question.
While debating motions, members of an assembly should address their remarks to the chair.

In large assemblies during the debate on motions, the presiding officer should not enter into debate on the pending uestions, should remain seated, and should not close debate if members wish to speak.
The chair can interrupt the speaker for any reason.
exp: The chair cannot interrupt the speaker unless that person violates a rule of the assembly or there is disorder.

q: When the presiding officer puts the question, this means that the chair is going to ask the maker of the motion a uestion.
exp: When the presiding officer puts the question, this means that the chair proceeds to take a vote on the pending motion.

q: The initial vote on a main motion in a large group is usually taken "viva voce," which means by voice.
exp: !n small groups, the initial vote may be taken by a show of hands.

q: The negative vote on a motion is always taken first by the presiding officer.
exp: The affirmative vote on a motion is always taken first by the presiding officer.

q: If the affirmative vote is almost unanimous on a motion that is complimentary and noncontroversial, the chair need not call for a negative vote.
When the chair takes a vote on a motion, the abstentions are called for last and used to calculate the majority number. f
exp: When the chair takes a vote on a motion, the abstentions are not taken.

q: If the following statement is used for taking a voice vote, the chair did not state the negative cue.PRESIDENT:-(Standing) "As many as are in favor of the motion, say ‘Aye. (Pause for response) "Opposed?"
The chair may take an affirmative vote by saying, "All those in favor say aye," "As many as are in favor, Say aye," or Those in favor of the motion, say aye."
The simple rising vote where the number of members voting on each side is not counted is usually used on motions requiring a two-thirds vote for adoption.
If a rising vote is not decisive, a counted vote can only be ordered by the secretary to make the minutes accurate.
exp: Ifa rising vote is not decisive, a counted vote can be ordered by the chair or the assembly.

q: If a rising vote is inconclusive, the chair should take another rising vote.
exp: if a rising vote is inconclusive, the chair should order another rising vote and order it to be counted. 98

q: A vote by a show of hands can be used to verify an inconclusive vote in any size group.
exp: A vote by a show of hands can be used in small groups.

q: Members have the right to change their vote up to the time the result is announced.
The chairs announcement of the result of a voice vote should include which side "has it," whether the motion is adopted or lost, and the effect of the vote.
When the vote on a motion is counted, the chair should state the count before announcing the prevailing side.
When announcing the affirmative results of a voice vote, the chair should say, "The ayes have it, and the motion is affirmed."
exp: When announcing the affirmative results of a voice vote, the chair should say, "The ayes have it, and the motion is adopted."

q: An example of an announcement by the chair after a rising vote on a motion has been taken and a count has been ordered could be, "There are 20 in the affirmative and 10 in the negative. The affirmative has it and the motion is adopted .. . "
For a motion requiring a two-thirds vote for adoption, the chair says, "There are less than two-thirds in the affirmative, and the motion is lost."
If there are 26 in the affirmative and 26 in the negative on a vote for a main motion, the chair would have to vote for the negative in order for the motion to be adopted.
exp: If there are 26 in the affirmative and 26 in the negative on a vote for a main motion, the chair would have to vote for the affirmative in order or the motion to be adopted.

q: The rising, counted vote on a main motion is 24 for the affirmative and 23 for the negative. The chair votes for the negative. This means that the vote on the main motion is a tie, and the main motion is adopted.
exp: The rising, counted vote on a main motion is 24 for the affirmative and 23 for the negative. The chair votes for the negative. This means that the vote on the main motion is a tie (24 affirmative and 24 negative), and the main motion is lost.

q: If the chair is in doubt about the close result of a voice vote, he/she should retake the vote by a division.
A demand of a member to retake a vote by rising is called a Division of the House.
exp: A demand of a member to retake a vote by rising is called a Division of the Assembly or "a division."

q: A member can demand a division from the moment the negative votes have been cast until the question is stated by the chair on another motion.
If a member wishes a voice vote to be retaken as a rising vote, he/she may cail out, without obtaining the floor, "I call or a division of the question."
exp: If a member wishes a voice vote to be retaken as a rising vote, he/she may call out, without obtaining the floor, "I doubt the result of the vote," "Division," or "I call for_a division."

q: One method of calling for a counted rising vote is for a member to rise, address the chair, and move that the vote be counted. This motion must be seconded and adopted by a two-thirds vote.
exp: One method of calling for a counted rising vote is for a member to rise, address the chair, and move that the vote be counted. This motion must be seconded and adopted by a maiority vote.

q: Suppose the chair has declared the results of a voice vote. A member who desires to have the vote taken again and counted should rise, address the chair, be recognized and say, "I move that the vote be counted."
In very small assemblies where everyone is easily seen, an inconclusive voice vote must be verified by a rising vote.
exp: In very small assemblies where everyone is easily seen, an inconclusive voice vote may be verified by a show of hands.

q: In very small assemblies, an inconclusive voice vote can be verified by a show of hands at the initiative of the chair.
In large assemblies, the chair has the same voting rights as any other member. This means that the chair may vote when it would affect the outcome, or may abstain.

If there is a tie vote on a motion and the chair abstains from voting, the chair should declare that the motion is adopted.§ 84. When there is one more vote in the affirmative than in the negative, and the chair votes in the negative, the motion is adopted.
exp: If there is a tie vote on a motion and the chair abstains from voting, the chair should declare that the motion is lost.

The primary purpose of using the subsidiary motion to Amend is to modify the wording of a pending motion.
When an amendment to a main motion is adopted, the motion that was amended is also adopted.
exp: When an amendment to a main motion is adopted, the motion that was amended remains pending and it may be debated.

q: Rejection of the subsidiary motion to Amend leaves the pending motion rejected also.
exp: Rejection of the subsidiary motion to Amend leaves the pending motion worded as it was before the amendment was made.

q: According to Robert's Rules of Order Newly Revised, the assembly "makes an amendment."
If a member votes in favor of the motion to Amend when the vote is taken on the motion to which the amendment applies, the member must also vote in favor of the amended motion.
exp: If a member votes in favor of the motion to Amend, when the vote is taken on the motion to which the amendment applies, the member s not obligated to vote in any particular way.

q: To be in order, an amendment must be germane.
exp: The amendment must relate to or have a bearing on the subject of the motion to be amended.

q: The subsidiary motion to Amend when applied to a main motion, takes precedence over the motion to Postpone ndefinitely.
The subsidiary motion to Amend can be applied to any main motion or any motion with a variable factor.
When the subsidiary motion to Amend is applied to itself, the result is an "amendment to an amendment," or a special subsidiary amendment.
exp: When the subsidiary motion to Amend is applied to itself, the result is an "amendment to an amendment," or a Secondary amendment.

q: The subsidiary motion to Amend can be postponed indefinitely.
exp: The subsidiary motion to Amend cannot be postponed indefinitely.

q: The subsidiary motion to Amend must be seconded in order to be considered.
A primary amendment applied to a main motion is not debatable.
exp: A primary amendment to a main motion is debatable whenever the motion to which it applies is debatable.

q: When an amendment is pending, the motion to be amended may be discussed.
exp: When an amendment is pending, the motion to be amended may not be discussed.

q: An amendment can be applied to itself.
If you were chair and a member moved to amend a Secondary Amendment, you should call the motion to amend the secondary amendment out of order.
An amendment to an amendment may be amended with the consent of the maker of the secondary amendment.
exp: An amendment to an amendment may not be amended.

q: An amendment to a primary amendment is called a secondary motion.
exp: An amendment to a primary amendment is called a secondary amendment.

q: The term prime amendment is preferred for an amendment to a main motion.
exp: The term primary amendment is preferred for an amendment to a main motion.

q: The term secondary amendment is preferred for an amendment to an amendment.
An amendment to the third degree is never permitted.
One primary amendment and one secondary amendment are allowed at a time.
The minimum affirmative vote necessary to adopt an amendment, even if the motion to be amended requires a two- thirds vote to be adopted, is two-thirds.
exp: The minimum affirmative vote necessary to adopt an amendment, even if the motion to be amended requires a two-thirds vote to be adopted, is a majority.

q: The process used to amend a motion by placing words at the end of a sentence is to add.
The process to fill a blank with words is not a form of amendment.
The form of amendment to Strike out would be proper to use if you wanted to strike out a paragraph and insert another paragraph.
exp: The form of amendment to Substitute would be a proper form to use if you wanted to strike out a paragraph and insert another paragraph.

q: The three basic processes of amendment (insert words, to strike out words, and to strike out and insert words) can be used to change the wording within a single sentence.
An amendment must be germane to be in order. This means that the date and purpose of the proposed change must be included.
exp: An amendment must be germane to be in order. This means that an amendment must in some way relate to the motion to which it is applied.

q: A motion is before the assembly "to commend' the high school basketball coach for her conduct during the disturbance after a recent game. After obtaining the floor, a member moves "to amend this motion by striking out ‘commend' and nserting in its place 'censure.™" The chair should then accept this amendment and ask for a second.
If the chair cannot decide if an amendment is germane, he/she would ask the maker to withdraw the amendment.
exp: If the chair cannot decide if an amendment is germane, he/she would refer the decision to the assembly and have them vote to determine if it is germane.

q: You are chair and a member moved "to postpone the question until 1 p.m." After this motion was seconded, another member then moved to amend the motion by "striking out ‘until 1 p.m.' and inserting 'indefinitely." You should process the amendment as stated.
exp: You are chair and a member moved "to postpone the question until 1 p.m.* After this motion was seconded, another member then moved to amend the motion by ‘striking out ‘until 1 p.m.' and inserting ‘indefinitely."" You should rule the amendment out of order because t would change the main question to a different kind of motion (to Postpone indefinitely.)

q: An amendment is always out of order that is frivolous or absurd.
One form of amending is to insert. This means that a word to be inserted is always placed at the end of the motion.
exp: One form of amending is to insert. This means that a word to be inserted is always placed between other words. The form to add is used to place a word or phrase at the end of a motion.

q: Suppose that the motion "to buy basketballs" is pending. A correct example of amending this motion by inserting is to say, "I move to amend by inserting the word 'three."
exp: Suppose that the motion "to buy basketbalis" is pending. A correct example of amending this motion by inserting is to say, "I move to amend by inserting the word ‘three' before the word ‘basketballs.

q: Assume the main motion "that we have a dance next Saturday" is pending. If you wanted to include the time for the dance, you would obtain the floor and say, "I move to amend by inserting ‘from 9 p.m. to 11:30 p.m."
exp: Assume the main motion "that we have a dance next Saturday" is pending. If you wanted to include the time for the dance, you would obtain the floor and say, "I move to amend by adding the words, ‘from 9 p.m. to 11:30 p.m."

q: If you were the presiding officer, the next step you would pursue after an amendment to a main motion is adopted would be debate on the amended main motion.
The motion to amend can be adopted without a formal vote (by unanimous consent).
exp: Amendments may be so simple or acceptable that they may be adopted by unanimous consent.

q: In amending a motion by striking out separate words, the best method is to make a motion to strike out the entire clause containing the separated words and insert a new clause.
A substitute motion offered for a main motion is an incidental main motion.
exp: A substitute motion offered for a main motion is a primary amendment.

q: When a primary amendment to a main motion is made to substitute, debate may go only into the merits of the primary amendment.
exp: When a primary amendment to a main motion is made to substitute, debate may go totally into the merits of the main motion.

q: After a section of a resolution has been substituted for another, the substituted section can be amended by adding.
A motion to Create a Blank can only be adapted to motions containing names of places.
exp: A motion to Create a Blank can only be adapted to motions containing names of persons, names of places, or amounts.

q: A blank to be filled can be created by a member offering a motion containing a blank, a member moving that a blank be created, or the chair making a suggestion that a blank be created.
The motion to Create a Blank is a main motion.
exp: The motion to Create a Blank is an incidental motion.

q: The motion to Create a Blank does not require a second.
exp: The motion to Create a Blank requires a second.

q: When the presiding officer recognizes that creating a blank on a pending main motion will facilitate the processing of a motion, he or she should suggest the creation of a blank and ask for unanimous (general) consent.
Each proposal for a blank may be debated and is handled as a separate original to be voted on individually until one s approved by a minimum affirmative vote of two-thirds.
exp: Each proposal for a blank may be debated and is handled as a separate original motion to be voted on individually until one is approved by a minimum affirmative vote of a majority.

q: A blank can be filled with names, amounts of money, or places, dates, or numbers.
One rule for filling in a blank with a name is that a majority vote is required to adopt the name that is proposed to fill n the blank.
If $125,000, $145,000, $149,000, and $151,000 are offered in filling a blank related to spending money, $151,000 should be considered first.
exp: Voting is from the highest to the lowest amount of money.

q: The vote that fills a blank decides the main motion.
exp: The main motion is normally decided after a blank is filled.

q: The purpose of the subsidiary motion to Commit or Refer is to send a pending question to a committee so that the uestion may be carefully investigated thoroughly and put into better condition for the assembly to consider.
The chief advantage of committees is that they allow greater freedom of debate on motions. This means that members can speak up to three times on each topic during a committee meeting.
exp: The chief advantage of committees is that they allow greater freedom of debate on motions. This means that members can speak as many times as they wish during a committee meeting.

q: To "consider informally," to "go into a committee of the whole," and to "go into a quasi committee of the whole" are all variations of the motion to Commit.
The term recommit is applied to a motion if the original motion to Commit (or refer) is lost.
exp: The term recommit is applied to a motion that proposes to refer a motion a second time.

q: The subsidiary motion to Commit (or Refer) takes precedence over the motion to Amend.
exp: _.mC

q: The subsidiary motion to Refer to a Committee can be applied to Main Motions.
The subsidiary motion to Commit (or Refer) cannot be applied to main motions with any amendments that may be pending.
exp: The motion to Commit (or Refer) can be applied to main motions with any amendments that may be pending.

q: The subsidiary motion to Commit (or Refer) can be postponed indefinitely.
exp: The subsidiary motion to Commit (or Refer) cannot be postponed indefinitely.

q: One of the rules concerning the subsidiary motion to Commit (or Refer) is that debate can pertain only to the desirability of committing the main question.
exp: Debate may not go into the merits of the main motion proposed to be committed (or referred)

q: The minimum affirmative vote required to adopt the subsidiary motion to Commit (or Refer) is two-thirds and previous notice.
exp: The minimum affirmative vote required to adopt the subsidiary motion to Commit (or Refer) is a majority.

q: If a motion is adopted to send the main question to a standing committee, the motion should indicate the name of the committee.

If the main question is to be handled by a special committee (select or ad hoc), the subsidiary motion to Commit (or Refer) may specify the number of committee members, method of selection, or the names of the members.
An example of binding instructions which may be included in the motion to Commit (or Refer) is how the committee should vote.
exp: When the committee should report, how the committee should consider the question, and if the committee should employ an expert consultant are all examples of binding instructions which may be included in the motion to Commit (or Refer).

q: A special committee appointed with "full power" means that the committee can act for the society in all future cases that are similar.
exp: A special committee appointed with "full power means that the committee can act for the society in a specific case. 103

q: A committee that is given "full power" to act for an organization can be authorized in a specific case to act for the society.

Suppose you were chair at a regular monthly meeting and a motion requiring action the next day was pending. a member moved to "refer the pending motion to a committee to report back at the next regular meeting," you would P rule the motion to refer is dilatory.
If an incomplete motion is made such as "to refer the main motion to a committee," the chair can call for amendments to complete the details.
exp: Examples of details are when it should report, and when the committee will meet.

q: Assume a main motion is pending. A member moves "to refer the main question to a committee." If suggestions are made by the assembly for different types of committees, the chair should take the vote on the committee of the whole rst.

If different methods such as viva voce, nominations from the floor, election by ballot, and appointment by the chair are suggested or moved on how to select a committee, election by ballot is voted on first.
All the names of nonmembers appointed to special or standing committees by the chair must be submitted for approval to the chair of each special committee and standing committee.
exp: All the names of nonmembers appointed to special or standing committees by the chair must be submitted for approval to the assembly.

q: If the chair appoints a committee, the committee members determine its chair.
exp: The chair who appoints a committee, determines its chair.

q: When a presiding officer appoints a committee at a regular meeting, the chair is usually the committee member named last.
exp: When a presiding officer appoints a committee at a regular meeting, the chair is usually the committee member named first.

q: The vice-president chooses the committee chair if the committee is not named by the chair.
exp: The assembly that elected the committee members chooses the committee chair if the committee is not named by the chair.

q: If the motion to Postpone Indefinitely is made before a member moved to refer a main motion to a committee, as chair you would declare that the motion to Postpone Indefinitely cannot be considered.
exp: The motion to Postpone indefinitely can only be applied to a main motion.

q: When a vacancy occurs in a committee that was selected by the president, vacancies are filled by the chair of the committee.
exp: When a vacancy occurs in a committee that was selected by the president, vacancies are filled by the president..

q: The form for the subsidiary motion to Commit (or Refer) is, "I move to commit and refer the motion to a committee."
exp: One form for the subsidiary motion to Commit (or Refer) is, "I move to refer the motion to a committee."

q: The form, "I move to commit or refer," is not correct for the subsidiary motion to Commit (or Refer).
If a main motion is pending that you feel needs to be studied further, you should obtain the floor and say, "Il move that the main motion be referred to a committee to be appointed by the chair."
exp: The number of members, the appointing power, when it shall report, etc. may be included in the motion.

q: The expressions Postpone, Postpone Definitely, and Postpone to a Certain Time can all be used to put off action on a pending motion.
section: 14. Postpone To A Certain Time (Or Definitely)

q: The subsidiary motion to Postpone to a Certain Time has the same effect as the motion to Postpone Indefinitely.
section: 14. Postpone To A Certain Time (Or Definitely)
exp: The subsidiary motion to Postpone to a Certain Time has the effect of postponing a motion to a certain time while the motion to Postpone ndefinitely kills a motion.

q: When a member proposes to postpone business that is not pending, it is a privileged motion.
section: 14. Postpone To A Certain Time (Or Definitely)
exp: When a member proposes to postpone business that is not pending, it is an incidental main motion.

q: The subsidiary motion to Postpone to a Certain Time can be made while the main motion with an amendment is pending.
section: 14. Postpone To A Certain Time (Or Definitely)

q: The subsidiary motion to Postpone to a Certain Time does not take precedence over the motion to Amend.
section: 14. Postpone To A Certain Time (Or Definitely)
exp: The subsidiary motion to Postpone to a Certain Time takes precedence over the motion to Amend.

q: The subsidiary motion to Postpone to a Certain Time (Postpone Definitely) yields to the motion to Lay on the Table.
section: 14. Postpone To A Certain Time (Or Definitely)

q: The subsidiary motion to Postpone to a Certain Time can be postponed indefinitely, committed, or laid on the table alone.
section: 14. Postpone To A Certain Time (Or Definitely)
exp: The subsidiary motion to Postpone to a Certain Time cannot be postponed indefinitely, committed, or laid on the table alone.

q: One rule for the subsidiary motion to Postpone to a Certain Time is that it is in order when another member has the oor.
section: 14. Postpone To A Certain Time (Or Definitely)
exp: The subsidiary motion to Postpone to a Certain Time is out of order when another member has the floor.

q: The subsidiary motion to Postpone to a Certain Time is debatable.
section: 14. Postpone To A Certain Time (Or Definitely)

q: The motion to Postpone to a Certain Time, is amendable and may be reconsidered.
section: 14. Postpone To A Certain Time (Or Definitely)

q: The subsidiary motion to Postpone to a Certain Time is amendable as to the location where the postponement will be considered.
section: 14. Postpone To A Certain Time (Or Definitely)
exp: The subsidiary motion to Postpone to a Certain Time is amendable as to the time that the main question may be postponed to.

q: In an assembly that does not meet as often as quarterly, a question cannot be postponed beyond the end of the next session.
section: 14. Postpone To A Certain Time (Or Definitely)
exp: In an assembly that does not meet as often as quarterly, a question cannot be postponed beyond the end of the present session.

q: In an organization that conducts its regular business meetings on the same day of each week, a question cannot be postponed for longer than a quarter (about three months).
section: 14. Postpone To A Certain Time (Or Definitely)
exp: In an organization that conducts its regular business meetings on the same day each week, a question cannot be postponed for longer than a week.

q: In an assembly that meets as often as quarterly, a question cannot be postponed beyond the end of the next session.
section: 14. Postpone To A Certain Time (Or Definitely)

q: The subsidiary motion to Postpone to a Certain Time does not have the same effect as the motion to Postpone ndefinitely.
section: 14. Postpone To A Certain Time (Or Definitely)

q: Assume a main motion is pending "that we play volleyball tonight." A member then moves "that we postpone the motion to play volleyball until tomorrow." As chair, you would rule the motion out of order.
section: 14. Postpone To A Certain Time (Or Definitely)

q: lf you are chair and a member wanted to postpone the officer reports and the committee reports, you should suggest that a motion be made to postpone each one as it is called for.
section: 14. Postpone To A Certain Time (Or Definitely)

q: When the bylaws require the election of officers at a specific meeting, a pending election can be postponed after first adopting a motion to Adjourn.
section: 14. Postpone To A Certain Time (Or Definitely)
exp: When the byiaws require the election of officers at a specific meeting, a pending election can be postponed after first adopting a motion to Fix the Time to Which to Adjourn.

q: If the subsidiary motion to Postpone Definitely is adopted, it always makes a postponed question an order of the day or a future meeting.
section: 14. Postpone To A Certain Time (Or Definitely)
exp: The motion to Postpone Definitely, if adopted, makes a postponed question an order of the day for the time to which it was postponed.

q: Orders of the day include general orders and special orders.
section: 14. Postpone To A Certain Time (Or Definitely)

q: General orders are taken up immediately after new business.
section: 14. Postpone To A Certain Time (Or Definitely)
exp: General orders are taken up immediately after unfinished business.

q: If business that has been postponed to a meeting is not disposed of before adjournment, it generally is laid on the table.
section: 14. Postpone To A Certain Time (Or Definitely)
exp: If business that has been postponed to a meeting is not disposed of before adjournment, it generally is considered as part of unfinished business at the next regular meeting.

q: When a main motion is postponed while a motion to Amend is pending, the amendment is lost.
section: 14. Postpone To A Certain Time (Or Definitely)
exp: When a main motion is postponed while a motion to Amend is pending, the amendment is postponed with the main motion.

q: When an amendment is taken up on a different day from the one on which it was proposed, each member cannot debate if they have already spoken twice at the previous meeting.
section: 14. Postpone To A Certain Time (Or Definitely)
exp: When an amendment is taken up on a different day from the one on which it was proposed, each member can again debate twice.

q: When a Main Motion is taken up again on a different day after it has been Postponed to a Certain Time, each member can speak on the Main Motion twice again.
section: 14. Postpone To A Certain Time (Or Definitely)

q: If you wanted to make sure a question will be considered at the next meeting and that it will not be crowded out by other business, the motion to make would be, "I move that the question be postponed to the next meeting and be made a special order."32
section: 14. Postpone To A Certain Time (Or Definitely)

q: The proper form to use to make a motion come up exactly at a certain hour even if it interrupts business that may be pending is, "I move that the motion be postponed and be made a special order for 3 p.m. tomorrow."
section: 14. Postpone To A Certain Time (Or Definitely)

q: If a main motion is pending that you feel should be put off until the next meeting, you should obtain the floor and say, move to postpone the main motion indefinitely to our next regular meeting."
section: 14. Postpone To A Certain Time (Or Definitely)
exp: Ifa main motion is pending that you feel should be put off until the next meeting, you should obtain the floor and say, "I move to postpone the main motion to our next regular meeting."

q: The subsidiary motions to Limit or Extend Limits of Debate and the Previous Question are not allowed in committees.
section: 15. Limit Or Extend Limits Of Debate

q: The subsidiary motion to Limit or Extend Limits of Debate may be used to reduce the length of speeches permitted, reduce the number of speeches permitted, or to close debate at a certain time.
section: 15. Limit Or Extend Limits Of Debate

q: The subsidiary motion to Limit or Extend Limits of Debate can force an instant closing of debate.
section: 15. Limit Or Extend Limits Of Debate
exp: The subsidiary motion to Limit or Extend Limits of Debate cannot force an immediate closing of debate. A motion for the Previous Question s used to close debate immediately.

q: An order limiting or extending the limits of debate that is no longer in force is said to be "expired."
section: 15. Limit Or Extend Limits Of Debate
exp: An order limiting or extending the limits of debate that is no longer in force is said to be "exhausted.°

q: The subsidiary motion to Limit or Extend Limits of Debate takes precedence over all debatable motions.
section: 15. Limit Or Extend Limits Of Debate

q: The subsidiary motion to Limit or Extend Limits of Debate can be applied to any immediately pending debatable motion.
section: 15. Limit Or Extend Limits Of Debate

q: The minimum affirmative vote needed to adopt the motion to Limit or Extend Limits of Debate when it is made with no uestion pending, is a majority.
section: 15. Limit Or Extend Limits Of Debate
exp: The minimum affirmative vote needed to adopt the motion to Limit or Extend Limits of Debate when it is made with no question pending, s two-thirds.

q: When the motion to Limit or Extend Limits of Debate is applied to a main motion, it can be laid on the table along with the main motion.
section: 15. Limit Or Extend Limits Of Debate

q: The subsidiary motion to Limit or Extend Limits of Debate is amendable.
section: 15. Limit Or Extend Limits Of Debate

q: Any amendment applied to the subsidiary motion to Limit or Extend Limits of Debate is debatable.
section: 15. Limit Or Extend Limits Of Debate
exp: Any amendment applied to the subsidiary motion to Limit or Extend Limits of Debate is undebatable.

q: The main reason that the motion to Limit or Extend Limits of Debate requires a two-thirds vote is because it is two, separate motions.
section: 15. Limit Or Extend Limits Of Debate
exp: The main reason that the motion to Limit or Extend Limits of Debate requires a two-thirds vote is because it takes away the rights of members to enter into free discussions.

q: Assume three debatable motions are pending. If a motion "to limit debate to two minutes per member" is adopted, only the immediately pending motion will be affected.
section: 15. Limit Or Extend Limits Of Debate
exp: The immediately pending motion is the last motion made. 104

q: If you were chair and a member proposed an Amendment to the main motion when the motion to Limit or Extend Limits of Debate was pending, you should call the amendment out of order.
section: 15. Limit Or Extend Limits Of Debate

q: If a motion to close debate in ten minutes is adopted, it is then in order to move to refer the matter to a committee.
section: 15. Limit Or Extend Limits Of Debate
exp: Ifa motion to close debate in ten minutes is adopted, it is not then in order to move to refer the matter to a committee.

q: Assume you are chair and a motion "to extend debate to fifteen minutes per member" is adopted. If a motion to call or the Previous Question is then made during regular debate, you should ask for debate on the Previous Question after t is seconded, and then take a standing vote.
section: 15. Limit Or Extend Limits Of Debate
exp: Assume you are chair and a motion "to extend debate to fifteen minutes per member" is adopted. If a motion to call for the Previous Question is properly made during regular debate, you should take a vote on the Previous Question aiter itis seconded. The motion for the Previous Question is not debatable.

q: An order limiting or extending limits of debate is exhausted when the questions affected by the order have been referred to a committee, when the meeting ends, or when questions on which it was applied have been all voted on.
section: 15. Limit Or Extend Limits Of Debate

q: Suppose debate on a motion is dragging on. If you wanted to reduce the number of times each member could debate to one time for each member, you should rise, and without obtaining the floor say, "I move to limited debate."33
section: 15. Limit Or Extend Limits Of Debate
exp: Suppose debate on a motion is dragging on. If you wanted to reduce the number of times each member could debate, you should obtain the floor and say, "I move that debate be limited to one speech for each member."

q: Unless the motion to Limit or Extend Limits of Debate is adopted by unanimous consent, the chair puts it to a vote by the raising of hands in a large group.
section: 15. Limit Or Extend Limits Of Debate
exp: Unless the motion to Limit or Extend Limits of Debate is adopted by unanimous consent, in a large group the chair puts it to a vote by sing. A rising vote should be used for a two-thirds vote requirement. 4. TRUE. The motion to Lay on the Table has a higher precedence than the Previous Question.

q: The Privileged Question is a motion to use at a meeting to stop debate immediately and vote on a pending question.
exp: The motion to call for the Previous Question would be used at a meeting to stop debate immediately and vote on a pending question.

q: If adopted, the Previous Question is a motion that only stops debate on the pending question.
exp: If adopted, the Previous Question is a motion that stops debate and the making of amendments on the pending question.

q: The Previous Question is allowed in committees.
exp: The Previous Question is not allowed in committees.

q: The subsidiary motion for the Previous Question takes precedence over the subsidiary motion to Limit or Extend Limits of Debate.
The Previous Question is a motion that does not prevent the making of privileged or incidental motions.

The subsidiary motion for the Previous Question can be applied to debatable or amendable motions that are immediately pending, and to any consecutive part of a series beginning with the immediately pending question.
The subsidiary motion for the Previous Question can be applied to an undebatable motion if a member wanted to stop an amendment.
exp: An example of an undebatable but amendable motion it can be applied to is to Limit or Extend Limits of Debate.

q: The unqualified form of the Previous Question can apply only to the immediately pending motion.
When the subsidiary motion for the Previous Question is made in its unqualified form such as "I move the previous uestion," this means that it applies to all pending questions.
exp: When the subsidiary motion for the Previous Question is made in its unqualified form such as "I move the previous question," this means that it applies only to the immediately pending question.

q: When the subsidiary motion for the Previous Question is immediately pending, it can be proposed again to include more or less pending questions.
If ninety votes are cast at a regular meeting on a motion for the Previous Question, the minimum number of affirmative votes that would be required to adopt it would be forty-six.
exp: Ifninety votes are cast at a regular meeting on a motion to Move the Previous Question, the minimum number of affirmative votes that would be required to adopt it would be sixty (It requires a two-thirds vote).

q: If a motion for the Previous Question fails to gain the necessary votes, debate is stopped on it.
exp: Ifa motion for the Previous Question fails to gain the necessary votes, debate continues on the pending motion as if this motion had not been made. The motion for the Previous Question is not debatable.

q: The rules of the United States House of Representatives permit the Previous Question to be adopted by a minimum affirmative vote of a majority.
If you wanted to close debate immediately, the form to be used after obtaining the floor could be, "I call for the uestion," "I call the question," or "I move we vote now."
A motion such as "I move we vote now," is not subject to the same rules of debate as the motion for the Previous Question.
exp: A motion such as "I move we vote now," is subject to all the rules as a motion for the Previous Question.

q: If a member obtained the floor and "called for the question" on a motion to Commit (or Refer), as chair you should make sure it is seconded.
When the Previous Question is ordered on a series of pending motions, they are voted on in the same order in which they were made.
exp: When the Previous Question is ordered on a series of pending motions, they are voted on in the reverse order in which they were made.

q: The Previous Question is said to be exhausted after all the motions on which it was ordered have been disposed of.
A vote that has ordered the Previous Question can be reconsidered at any time.
exp: A vote that has ordered the Previous Question can be reconsidered before any of the motions affected by the order have been voted on.

q: When using the form "I move the previous question," it applies to all pending questions.
exp: When using the form "I move the previous question," it applies to only the immediatel nding question.

q: To properly call for the Previous Question, members should call out "Question" from their seats without being recognized.
exp: To properly call for the Previous Question members should say "I move the previous question" afle? Obt question' after obtaining the floor.

q: As the chair, you should call for a vote on the amendment after the motion for the Previous Question is adopted on t.
The motion to Lay on the Table allows an assembly to lay a pending question aside permanently when something else of immediate urgency has arisen.
exp: The motion to Lay on the Table allows an assembly to lay a pending question aside temporarily when something else of immediate urgency has arisen.

q: The motion to Lay on the Table sets the pending question aside temporarily and there is no set time for taking up the matter again.
exp: A motion to Take From the Table must be used to take up the motion again.

q: The motion to Lay on the Table is sometimes misused in meetings in place of the motion to Commit (or Refer).
exp: The motion to Lay on the Table is sometimes misused in meetings in place of the motion to Postpone to a Certain Time.

q: If a member proposed the motion to Lay on the Table and specified a time for resuming consideration, as chair you should suggest that the maker of the motion submit it as a Motion to Postpone.
A subsidiary motion to Lay on the Table takes precedence over all motions.
exp: A subsidiary motion to Lay on the Table takes precedence over all subsidiary motions.

q: The motion to Lay on the Table is out of order if the intent is to kill a motion.
exp: This motion is sometimes used incorrectly in the place of the motion to Posipone indefinitely.

q: Ifa main motion and a primary amendment are pending, and a motion to lay the main motion on the table is adopted, the amendment itself dies and is taken up under unfinished business at the next regular meeting.
exp: Ifa main motion and a primary amendment are pending, and a motion to lay the main motion on the table is adopted, the amendment tself adheres to the main motion.

q: Subsidiary motions cannot be applied to the motion to Lay on the Table.
The motion to Lay on the Table can be applied only to a question that is pending.
The motion to Lay on the Table may be made when another member has the floor.
exp: The motion to Lay on the Table is out of order when another member has the floor.

q: The maker of the motion to Lay on the Table may never state the reason prior to proposing it.
exp: The maker of the motion may state the reason prior to proposing the motion to Lay onthe Table.

q: The motion to Lay on the Table can be made when the Previous Question has been made.
The subsidiary motion to Lay on the Table cannot be qualified in any manner.
The motion to Lay on the Table can be amended.
exp: The motion to Lay on the Table cannot be amended.

q: The subsidiary motion to Lay on the Table can sometimes have the negative vote sometimes be reconsidered.
One of the rules related to the motion to Take From the Table is that it requires a majority vote for its adoption.
A question can be taken from the table at a special meeting only if permitted by the chair.
exp: A question can be taken from the table at a special meeting if previous notice of such intention was indicated in the call of the meeting.

q: Laying a question on the table again the same day after substantial debate has transpired is not permissible.
exp: Laying a question on the table again the same day is in order after substantial debate has transpired.

q: In organizations that hold regular business sessions as often as quarterly, a question laid on the table remains there until taken from the table or until the end of the next special meeting.
exp: In organizations that hold regular business sessions as often as quarterly, a question laid on the table remains there until taken from the table or until the end of the next regular session.

q: It is out of order to move to lay a pending question on the table if there is no other matter requiring attention that is urgent.
The motion to Lay on the Table is often used incorrectly to set a motion aside in order to consider a non-urgent matter, to suppress a motion without debate, or to kill a motion without a vote on it.
At a special meeting, a motion cannot be made to lay on the table the matter for which the meeting was called.
The correct motion that should be used to dispose of a motion without a direct vote is to Lay on the Table.
exp: The correct motion that should be used to dispose of a motion without a direct vote is to Postpone indefinitely.

q: If a main motion is being debated and you become aware that something else of immediate urgency has arisen, you should obtain the floor and say, "I move to lay the question on the table."
The motion to Lay on the Table can be qualified as to the time the motion may be taken up again.
exp: The motion to Lay on the Table cannot be qualified in any way.

q: A member can also suggest its intended purpose when making the motion to Lay on the Table.
The privileged motion to Call for the Orders of the Day is used primarily to indicate to members when a point of order may be called.
section: 18. Call For The Orders Of The Day
exp: The privileged motion to Call for the Orders of the Day is used primarily to require that a meeting conform to its agenda.

q: The orders of the day can be called by any member.
section: 18. Call For The Orders Of The Day

q: The privileged motion to Call for the Orders of the Day takes precedence over all subsidiary motions.
section: 18. Call For The Orders Of The Day

q: The privileged motion to Call for the Orders of the Day can only be used by a member when the assembly varies from the agenda.
section: 18. Call For The Orders Of The Day
exp: The privileged motion to Call for the Orders of the Day can also be used when a member wishes the assembly to consider a general order that is in order at the time but is not being considered.

q: The privileged motion to Call for the Orders of the Day may not be seconded, debated, or amended.
section: 18. Call For The Orders Of The Day

q: The orders of the day can be set aside by any single member who objects.
section: 18. Call For The Orders Of The Day
exp: The orders of the day can be set aside by a two-thirds vote.

q: if an unwanted motion is made that deviates from the correct order of business, a Call for the Orders of the Day must be made before the question is put by the chair.
section: 18. Call For The Orders Of The Day
exp: [fa motion is made that deviates from the correct order of business, a Call for the Orders of the Day must be made before the motion is stated by the chair.

q: Assume you are chair at a meeting. The orders of the day are called for. If you sense that the assembly would prefer to consider the pending question, you should call for a vote on whether the assembly wishes to consider the orders of the day.
section: 18. Call For The Orders Of The Day

q: At his/her own initiative, the chair can put the question on proceeding with the orders of the day to the assembly. The minimum negative vote required to vote this motion down is a majority.
section: 18. Call For The Orders Of The Day
exp: At his/her own initiative, the chair.can put the question on proceeding with the orders of the day to the assembly. The minimum negative vote required to vote this motion down is two-thirds.

q: If an assembly refuses to go to the orders of the day, they cannot be called for again until the pending business is disposed of.
section: 18. Call For The Orders Of The Day

q: A member of a large assembly who calls for the orders of the day does not need to be recognized by the chair.
section: 18. Call For The Orders Of The Day

q: To call for the orders of the day, a member should rise, address the chair, and without being recognized, say, Order, Order! I rise to call for the orders of the day."
section: 18. Call For The Orders Of The Day
exp: To call for the orders of the day, a member should rise, and without being recognized, say, "Mr. or Madam President, I call for the orders of the day."

q: Suppose there is a meeting in progress and the assembly has digressed from the agenda to such an extent that the important items on the agenda may not be considered because of a lack of time. As a member you should rise, and without obtaining the floor say, "Mr. or Madam President, I call for the orders of the day."
section: 18. Call For The Orders Of The Day

q: The motion to Raise a Question of Privilege is a device which may permit action otherwise not in order.
Raising a question of privilege while business is pending requires recognition from the chair to state the request.
The motion to Raise a Question of Privilege takes precedence over the motion to Recess.
exp: The motion to Raise a Question of Privilege takes precedence over all motions except the higher ranking privileged motions.

q: A member who has been assigned the floor may be interrupted for the purpose of raising a question of privilege.
exp: The situation must be urgent and the member should not be actually speaking.

q: The privileged device, Raise a Question of Privilege, may be amended, debated, and requires a second.
exp: The privileged device, Raise a Question of Privilege is not amendable, debatable, or seconded.

q: The parliamentarian makes the initial ruling on the motion to Raise a Question of Privilege.
exp: The chair makes the initial ruling on the motion to Raise a Question of Privilege.

q: MEMBER:-(Rising, and without obtaining the floor) "I rise to a question of privilege affecting the assembly." The statement above can be used by a member at a meeting to request that specific windows be opened to increase the ventilation in the meeting room.
Charges circulated against a member's character would not be a topic to justify a member making a Question of Privilege affecting the assembly.
Assume you are the chair, and a member rises and addresses you without being recognized and says, "I rise to a uestion of personal privilege." You should then ask for a second.
exp: Assume you are the chair, and a member rises and addresses you without being recognized and says, "I rise to a question of personal privilege." You should then direct the member to state his/her question. of powiege if you feel it should be entertained.

q: If a motion is made as a question of privilege and it is seconded, as chair you should call the motion out of order.
exp: {f a motion is made as a question of privilege is Si , as chair, you should call for debate, and then vote on it.

q: Suppose the meeting hall is very noisy because of the construction of a new road next to the building. To try to solve the problem, you should rise, and without obtaining the floor say, "Mr. President, I rise to a question of privilege affecting the assembly."

At a regular meeting, a controversial matter that demands immediate action is introduced as a main motion. During debate a member interrupts, rises to a question of privilege, and moves "that the meeting be closed and that nonmembers be asked to leave." The chair should put the motion to an immediate vote.
exp: Ata regular meeting, a controversial matter that demands immediate action is introduced as a main motion. During debate, a member nterrupts, rises to a question of privilege, and moves "that the meeting be closed and that nonmembers be asked to leave." If the chair eels the meeting should be continued, it should be seconded and allowed to be debated.
