q: The privileged motion to Recess is used to take a brief intermission in an assembly's proceedings which closes the meeting for the day.
exp: The privileged motion to Recess is used to take a brief intermission in an assembly's proceedings which closes the meeting after which the meeting is continued precisely where it was interrupted.

q: A Recess may be taken only to allow for informal consultation.
exp: A Recess may be taken to allow for informal consultation, to count ballots, and to secure information.

q: When a motion to recess is made while another motion is pending, it is a main motion.
exp: When a motion to recess is made while another motion is pending, it is a privileged motion.

q: The privileged motion to Recess is a motion that a recess begin when the member who proposed the pending motion grants permission.
exp: The privileged motion to Recess is a motion that a recess begin immediately.

q: A motion to recess that is made when no business is pending is a privileged motion.
exp: A motion to recess that is made when no business is pending is a main motion.

q: The privileged motion to Recess is "privileged" only when it is proposed while another question is pending.

Assume a main motion is pending at a regular meeting. A member gains the floor and moves "that the assembly recess or dinner after the vote on the pending motion." As chair, you should take a voice vote on the motion to recess without a second.
exp: Assume a main motion is pending at a regular meeting. A member gains the floor and moves that the assembly recess for dinner after the vote on the pending motion. The chair should declare the motion to recess out of order because it is another main motion.

q: The motion to take a recess at a future time may be proposed only when another question is pending.
exp: The motion to take a Recess at a future time may be proposed when no question is pending.

q: The privileged motion to Recess has precedence over the motion to Refer to a Committee.
The privileged motion to Recess is not amendable.
exp: The privileged motion to Recess is amendable as to the length of the recess.

q: An amendment to the privileged motion to Recess is debatable.
exp: An amendment to the privileged motion to Recess is not debatabie.

q: The chair declares the recess at the specified time if it is provided for in an adopted agenda.
If a prescheduled recess is not announced by the chair at the scheduled time, a member should call for the orders of the day.
The time for taking a prescheduled recess can be postponed by a two-thirds vote of the people attending.
exp: The time for taking a prescheduled recess can be postponed by a two-thirds vote of the assembly.

q: If your organization is debating a motion and you want to talk privately to several fellow members about the business at hand, you should obtain the floor and say, "I move to recess for ten minutes."
The gavel should not be rapped to signal the adoption of a recess.
exp: The gavel may be rapped to signal a recess, an adjournment, and a breach of order.

q: Obtaining the floor and saying, "I move to adjoum" is an example of the privileged motion to Adjourn.
The privileged motion to Adjourn is always moved in an unqualified form, is used to close the meeting immediately, and s made when no time for adjourning has been set.
A motion to Adjourn is always privileged when the time for adjournment has been set.
exp: A motion to Adjoum is always privileged when no time for adjournment has been set (is unqualified).

q: If the motion to Adjourn is made in the form of "I! move to adjourn" when no question is pending, it is debatable.
exp: If the motion to Adjourn is made in the form of "I move to adjoum" when no question is pending, it is not debatable.

q: If a motion to adjourn is qualified in any way, it is classified as a privileged motion.
exp: If a motion to adjoum is qualified in any way, it is classified as a main motion.

q: A motion to Adjourn at or to a future time while business is pending is always out of order.
A motion "to adjourn" is always a privileged motion when not qualified.
The privileged motion to Adjourn takes precedence over all motions except the privileged motion to Recess.
exp: The privileged motion to Adjourn takes precedence over all.motions except the privileged motion to Fix the Time to Which to Adjourn.

q: The privileged motion to Adjourn is not in order while the assembly is engaged in voting by voice.
When the privileged motion to Adjourn is pending, the privileged motion to Recess is in order.
exp: When the privileged motion to Adjourn is pending, the privileged motion to Fix the Time to Which to Adjoum is in order. 41. FALSE. The privileged motion to Adjoum can be applied to no other motions.

q: The privileged motion to Adjourn does not need to be seconded.
exp: The privileged motion to Adjourn must be seconded.

q: The minimum affirmative vote necessary to adopt the privileged motion to Adjourn is a majority.
If a motion to Adjourn is defeated, any member who voted on the affirmative side may move to reconsider the vote.
exp: If a motion to Adjourn is defeated, no one may move to reconsider the vote.

q: If a question is pending at an organized monthly meeting and an adjournment closed the meeting, the pending motion s lost.
exp: If a question is pending at an organized monthly meeting and an adjournment closed the meeting, the pending motion is taken up as the rst item under unfinished business at the next monthly meeting.

q: A motion to close the session of an assembly and dissolve it is referred to as a motion to "adjourn sine die," which means to "adjourn for one day."
exp: A motion to close the session of an assembly and dissolve it is referred to as a motion to "adjourm sine die," which means to "adjourn without day."

q: After a committee of the whole has accomplished the business that was referred to it, the committee "rises" and reports, which is the same as the main motion to adjourn.
The privileged motion to Adjourn may be held pending while the assembly is informed of business requiring immediate attention.
While the privileged motion to Adjoum is pending, it is not in order to make a main motion.
When the privileged motion to Adjourn is pending, members may give notice of a motion that will be made at the next meeting.
Until the chair has taken the negative vote on the motion to Adjourn, a meeting is not adjourned.
exp: A meeting is not closed by a motion to Adjoum until the chair has stated that the meeting ‘is adjourned."

q: A motion to adjourn that has obviously been made for obstructive purposes should be referred to the assembly by the chair for debate.
exp: A motion to adjourn that has obviously been made for obstructive purposes should be refused to be entertained by the chair.

q: If you are the chair at a regular meeting and a member calls out, "I move to adjourn" without obtaining the floor, you could process the motion by unanimous consent.
Assume you are chair at a convention and the time has arrived for a prescheduled adjournment. You should immediately ask for a motion to adjourn from any member of the assembly.
exp: Assume you are chair at a convention and the time has arrived for a prescheduled adjournment. You should announce the fact and declare the meeting adjourned.

q: The privileged motion to Adjourn is not needed if the chair adjourns a meeting after asking for further business.
If it appears that there is no further business in a meeting of an ordinary society, the chair needs only to state, "The meeting is adjourned."
exp: If it appears that there is no further business in a meeting of an ordinary society, the chair should state, "Is there any further business? (Silence) Since there is no further business, the meeting is adjourned."

q: "I move to adjourn," "I move that we now adjourn to meet at 6 p.m. on May 5," and "I move that the meeting adjourn" are all correct forms for making the motion to adjourn as a main motion.
exp: Only the form that sets a time to meet again ("adjourn to meet at 6 p.m. on May 5") is a main motion; the plain forms are privileged motions.

q: Suppose it is 11:00 p.m. and there has been prolonged debate on the last, unimportant agenda item. You want the meeting to end. You should rise, and without obtaining the floor say, "I move to adjourn."
exp: Suppose it is 11:00 p.m. and there has been prolonged debate on the last, unimportant agenda item. You want the meeting to end. You should obtain the fioor and say, "I move to adjourn."

q: After a motion to Adjourn has been made and seconded when there is no other business, to adjourn the meeting by unanimous consent the chair should say, "If there is no objection, the meeting will now adjoum." (Pause for response) 5 (Silence) "Since there is no objection, the meeting is adjourned." (The gavel may be tapped once)
The purpose of the privileged motion to Fix the Time to Which to Adjourn is to establish a special meeting.
section: 22. Fix The Time To Which To Adjourn
exp: The purpose of the privileged motion to Fix the Time to Which to Adjoum is to establish an adjoumed meeting.

q: The motion to Fix the Time to Which to Adjourn has the effect of setting the time, and sometimes the place, for another meeting to continue the business of the meeting.
section: 22. Fix The Time To Which To Adjourn

q: The motion to Fix the Time to Which to Adjoum affects the time when the present meeting will adjourn.
section: 22. Fix The Time To Which To Adjourn
exp: The motion to Fix the Time to Which to Adjourn does not affect the time when the present meeting will adjourn.

q: Depending on the circumstances, the motion to Fix the Time to Which to Adjourn may be proposed as a privileged motion or a main motion.
section: 22. Fix The Time To Which To Adjourn

q: The motion to Fix the Time to Which to Adjourn is a privileged motion only if it is made when no question is pending.
section: 22. Fix The Time To Which To Adjourn
exp: The motion to Fix the Time to Which to Adjoum is a privileged motion only if it is made while a motion is pending and there is not a meeting scheduled for the same or next day.

q: If a motion to Fix the Time to Which to Adjourn is made when no question is pending, the chair should rule it out of order.
section: 22. Fix The Time To Which To Adjourn
exp: If a motion to Fix the Time to Which to Adjourn is made when no question is pending, it is subject to all the rules applicabie to a main motion.

q: If the motion To Fix The Time To Which To Adjourn is made at a meeting while no question is pending, it s debatable.
section: 22. Fix The Time To Which To Adjourn

q: The privileged motion to Fix the Time to Which to Adjoum yields to a Point of Order.
section: 22. Fix The Time To Which To Adjourn

q: The privileged motion to Fix the Time to Which to Adjoum is debatable.J °
section: 22. Fix The Time To Which To Adjourn
exp: The privileged motion to Fix the Time to Which to Adjoum is not debatable.

q: The privileged motion to Fix the Time to Which to Adjourn is amendable only as to the date.
section: 22. Fix The Time To Which To Adjourn
exp: The privileged motion to Fix the Time to Which to Adjoum is amendable as to the date, hour and place regarding a continuation of the present meeting.

q: If an amendment to the privileged motion to Fix the Time to Which to Adjourn is made and immediately seconded, your next step as chair would be to take a vote on the amendment.
section: 22. Fix The Time To Which To Adjourn
exp: The amendment is not debatable because the motion to Fix the Time to Which to Adjourn is not debatable.

q: The privileged motion to Fix the Time to Which to Adjourn takes precedence over all other motions, and the minimum affirmative vote necessary to adopt it is two-thirds.
section: 22. Fix The Time To Which To Adjourn
exp: The privileged motion to Fix the Time to Which to Adjoum does take precedence over all other motions, but the minimum affirmative vote necessary to adopt it is a majority.

q: MEMBER:-(After obtaining the floor) "I move that when this meeting adjourns, it adjourn to meet at 9 a.m. next Wednesday." The adoption of this motion establishes an adjourned meeting.
section: 22. Fix The Time To Which To Adjourn

q: The effect of adopting the privileged motion to Fix the Time to Which to Adjoum is to adjourn the present meeting.
section: 22. Fix The Time To Which To Adjourn
exp: The effect of adopting the privileged motion to Fix the Time to Which to Adjoum is to establish a continuation of the present meeting.

q: At an adjourned meeting, everything is taken up from the point at which the previous meeting adjourned except the minutes are read first.
section: 22. Fix The Time To Which To Adjourn

q: The adoption of the motion to Fix the Time to Which to Adjourn does not have the same effect as a motion to fix the time at which to adjourn.
section: 22. Fix The Time To Which To Adjourn

q: Suppose the assembly is debating a main motion and the hour is getting late. You want to make sure that the assembly meets again tomorrow to complete the agenda. You should obtain the floor and say, "I move that when this meeting adjourns, it adjourn to meet again at 9:00 a.m. tomorrow."41
section: 22. Fix The Time To Which To Adjourn

q: A Point of Parliamentary Inquiry could be made so that the chair would be called on to enforce a violated rule.
exp: A Point of Order could be made so that the chair would be called on to enforce a violated rule.

q: A Point of Order yields to all privileged motions.
If a Point of Order is raised while an amendment is immediately pending, the amendment is disposed of first, and the point of order next.
exp: Ifa Point of Order is raised while an amendment is immediately pending, the Point of Order is disposed of first.

q: A Point of Order should never interrupt a person debating a main motion.
exp: A Point of Order can interrupt a person debating a main motion.

q: After a member makes a Point of Order, the chair should always try to make a ruling on it.
When a member makes a Point of Order, it is normally ruled on by the parliamentarian.
exp: When a member makes a Point of Order, it is normally ruled on by the chair. 107

q: A Point of Order normally is voted on in all cases.
exp: A Point of Order normally is not voted on unless the chair is in doubt or the chairs tuling is appealed.

q: The normal grounds for a member to rise to a Point of Order are to obtain parliamentary information from the parliamentarian.
exp: The normal grounds for a member to rise to a Point of Order are a breach of rules.

q: Points of order should not be raised on all trivial irregularities that are very technical.
A member must make a Point of Order immediately after the member who made the breach is seated.
exp: A member must make a Point of Order as soon as the breach occurs.

q: A Point of Order would be proper to use if the presiding officer at your organization's meeting asked for debate on a main motion before it was seconded.
If a motion is not seconded, and is debated and then adopted, a point of order is too late.
If a member is unsure whether a speaker has broken a rule, the member may make a Parliamentary Inquiry.

Suppose a member at a meeting is debating the main motion while an amendment is the immediately pending uestion. To stop the member from speaking on the main motion, you would rise and without obtaining the floor say, rise to a point of order."
If you were chair, after a member makes a Point of Order, you should immediately ask the assembly for a second.
exp: If you were chair, after a member makes a Point of Order, you should immediately ask the member to "state your point."

q: When a member of an assembly states, "I rise to a point of order," the member who is speaking should immediately be seated.
After a member rises and states a point of order, he/she should remain standing while the chair makes a ruling.
exp: After a member rises and states a point of order, he/she should be seated.

q: After a member rises to a Point of Order and states his/her point, the chair immediately states if the member is "right" or "wrong."
exp: After a member rises to a Point of Order and states his/her point, the chair normally rules whether the "point of order is {is not) well taken," } and then states the reason.

q: The chair consults the vice-president if in doubt on how to rule on a point of order.r
exp: The chair consults the parliamentarian if in doubt on how to mule on a point of order.

q: If you were chair and were unsure on how to rule on a Point of Order, you could submit it to a vote of the assembly.
When a point of order that is submitted to a vote is debatable, no member of the assembly can debate more than once except the member who made the point of order.
exp: When a point of order that is submitted to a vote is debatable, no member of the assembly can debate more than once except the chair, J who can speak first and last.

q: An Appeal from the decision of the chair is a point of order stated in another way.
exp: An Appeal from the decision of the chair is a disagreement with the ruling of the chair.

q: The incidental motion to Appeal is used when an accurate standing vote is needed on a main motion.
exp: The incidental motion to Appeal is used to have the chairs ruling voted on by the assembly.

q: A characteristic of the motion to Appeal is that it yields to all privileged motions.
The chair's ruling can be appealed at any time.
exp: The chair's ruling must be appealed at the time of the ruling.

q: Assume you are chair and made a decision. Several members immediately speak on the pending motion and then a member appeals the decision you made earlier. You should rule that the appeal is too late,
The incidental motion to Appeal may interrupt a speaker and need not be seconded.
exp: The incidental motion to Appeal may not interrupt a speaker and must be seconded.

q: The incidental motion to Appeal is debatable unless it is made while the immediate pending question is undebatable, relates to indecorum or a transgression of the rules of speaking, or relates to priority of business.
When debating the motion to Appeal, the presiding officer must leave the chair.
exp: One unique feature about the motion to Appeal is that the presiding officer may enter into debate without giving up the chair.

q: When the incidental motion to Appeal is debatable, no member can speak more than once except the presiding officer, who may speak three times.
exp: When the incidental motion to Appeal is debatable, no member can speak more than once except the presiding officer, who may speak twice.

q: A tie vote on the motion to Appeal from the decision of the chair reverses the decision of the chair.
exp: A tie vote on the motion to Appeal from the decision of the chair sustains the decision of the chair.

q: When a member disagrees with the ruling of the chair on a Point of Order, a motion should be made to appeal the decision of the chair.
The chair's response to a parliamentary inquiry or to a request for information, and the chair's announcement of the results of a vote, are not subject to an Appeal.
exp: These are opinions, not rulings.

q: If you are chair and a member appeals your announcement of the results of a vote, you should take another voice vote.
exp: If you are chair and a member appeais your announcement of the results of a vote, you can suggest that the member should call for a Division.

q: If you do not agree with the chairs ruling on your Point of Order, you should rise, and without obtaining the floor say, appeal from the decision of the chair."
The proper language to use by the chair for putting the affirmative vote of the question on an appeal is, "all those in avor of my decision, say ‘aye.""
exp: The proper language to use by the chair for stating the affirmative vote of the question on an appeal is "as many as are in favor of sustaining the chair's decision, say ‘aye.'

q: When a member wishes to do something at a meeting that cannot be done without violating one or more of its regular rules, the assembly can adopt a motion to suspend the rules.
Local, state, or national laws may be suspended.
exp: Local, state, or national laws, the fundamental principles of parliamentary law, and rules protecting absentees may not be suspended.

q: The incidental motion to Suspend the Rules does not require a second.
exp: The incidental motion to Suspend the Rules must be seconded.

q: The incidental motion to Suspend the Rules usually is adopted by a two-thirds vote.
The object of the incidental motion to Suspend the Rules is to suspend one or more rules contained in the parliamentary authority, special rules of order, or standing rules of the assembly.
In making the motion to Suspend the Rules, the motion must state its specific purpose.
Unless unanimous consent is given, members cannot try to suspend the same rule that was voted down at the same meeting more than twice.
exp: Unless unanimous consent is given, members cannot try to suspend the same rule that was voted down at the same meeting more than once.

q: Rules that cannot generally be suspended are those that protect absentees and the basic rights of individual members and those in the bylaws (or constitution).
The rule that requires previous notice of a proposed amendment to the bylaws can be suspended by unanimous consent.
exp: The rule that requires previous notice of a proposed amendment to the bylaws cannot be suspended.

q: The minimum affirmative vote necessary to suspend rules of parliamentary procedure that are in an established parliamentary procedure manual is a majority.
exp: The minimum affirmative vote necessary to suspend rules of parliamentary procedure that are in an established parliamentary procedure manual is two-thirds.

q: The motion to Suspend the Rules would be used to dispense with the regular order of business and proceed to a subject that is scheduled tater in the meeting.
An established order of business previously adopted by the society cannot be suspended by a majority vote.
The standing rule of a local society which lists the time for beginning meetings can be suspended by a majority vote.
The minimum affirmative vote necessary to suspend Standing Rules is two-thirds without notice.
exp: The minimum affirmative vote necessary to suspend Standing Rules is a majority without notice.

q: If an original main motion is proposed that is strongly undesirable, you should make a motion to Dispense with the Question.
section: 26. Objection To The Consideration Of A Question
exp: An Objection to the Consideration of a Question may be proposed if an original main motion is strongly undesirable.

q: An Objection to the Consideration of the Question can be raised only before there has been any debate or any subsidiary motion has been stated by the chair.
section: 26. Objection To The Consideration Of A Question

q: An Objection to the Consideration of the Question can be applied to any motion stated.
section: 26. Objection To The Consideration Of A Question
exp: An Objection to the Consideration of the Question can be applied only to original main motions and to petitions and communications that are not from a superior body.

q: An Objection to the Consideration of a Question requires a two-thirds vote to sustain the objection.
section: 26. Objection To The Consideration Of A Question

q: The chair can make a motion to Object to the Consideration of a Question.
section: 26. Objection To The Consideration Of A Question

q: MEMBER:- (Rising, and without waiting to be recognized) "Mr. President, I object to the consideration of the motion." The effect of the above motion is to object to the fact that a motion has been considered and adopted by a majority vote.
section: 26. Objection To The Consideration Of A Question
exp: The effect of the motion is to not consider the immediately pending motion during the meeting.

q: If an objection to the consideration of a main motion is sustained, the main motion is dismissed for that session.
section: 26. Objection To The Consideration Of A Question

q: Suppose an undesirable main motion has been moved and seconded. At this stage, you can keep this motion from coming before the assembly by obtaining the floor and saying, "I move that this objectionable motion be tabled."
section: 26. Objection To The Consideration Of A Question
exp: Suppose an undesirable main motion has been moved and seconded. At this stage, you can keep this motion from coming before the assembly by obtaining the floor and saying, "I object to the consideration of the motion (or question' or 'resolution."

q: When a member raises an objection to the consideration of a question, the chair should state, "An objection has been raised. Is there any discussion?"
section: 26. Objection To The Consideration Of A Question
exp: When a member raises an objection to the consideration of a question, the chair should ask, "The consideration of the question is objected to. Shall the question be considered?. . ."

q: The motion calling for a Division of a Question is used to obtain a standing vote on the pending question.
exp: The motion calling for a Division of a Question is used to separate, debate, and vote on different, distinct parts of a motion.

q: When a motion is adopted for a Division of a Question, it means that the pending motion can be divided into separate parts for action.

MEMBER:-(After obtaining the floor) "I move that we buy our president a new lectern and a new gavel." You would use the motion for a Division of the Business in order to make the motion above two separate motions.
exp: You would use the motion for a Division of the Question in order to make the motion above two separate motions.

q: The incidental motion calling for a Division of the Question cannot be made on the main question while an amendment to the main question is pending.
The incidental motion for Division of a Question must be seconded and is not debatable.
Motions to divide amendments are never allowed.
exp: Motions to divide amendments are permissible.

q: Assume a member proposes a motion "to collect $10 from each member and give the money to the local high school." After a second, another member moves to divide the motion into two parts: "To collect $10 from each member," and give the money to the local high school." If you were chair, you should rule the motion out of order because the second half (part) cannot stand alone.
The motion, "I move we form a recreation committee and give it instructions," would be appropriate to be divided.
exp: The motion, "I move we form a recreation committee and give it instructions," cannot be divided into two parts that would stand alone, and would not be appropriate to be divided.

q: If a member is not in agreement with a portion of a main motion that is indivisible, the member can move to strike out the part that is unfavorable.
When a series of main motions that deal with different subjects is offered in one motion, a single member can request that each motion receive separate consideration.

Assume a member has proposed a motion "that we send our president and all the other officers to Hawaii." If you want to discuss "sending our president to Hawaii" and "sending all the other officers to Hawaii" separately, obtain the floor and say, "I move to divide the motion so as to consider separately the question of 'sending our president to Hawaii' ] and ‘sending all the other officers to Hawaii."

A long motion consisting of several paragraphs can be considered by proposing a motion to open different parts to debate without a division of the question. This motion is called Consideration by Paragraph or Series.
exp: Along motion consisting of several paragraphs can be considered by proposing a motion to open different parts to debate without a division of the question. This motion is called Consideration by Paragraph or Seriatim.

q: The incidental motion for Consideration by Paragraph or Seriatim requires a two-thirds vote.
exp: The incidental motion for Consideration by Paragraph or Seriatim requires a Majority vote.

q: When a document is considered by paragraph, a member cannot debate each paragraph.
exp: When a document is considered by paragraph, a member can debate each paragraph.

q: If the chair suggests consideration of a document by paragraph, and you wanted to save time by acting on the entire document, you should obtain the floor and say, "I move that it be considered as a whole."

A complicated resolution having several paragraphs is pending. You feel that it could be dealt with more efficiently if each paragraph could be handled separately. From your seat, and without obtaining the floor, you should say, "Division!"45
exp: A complicated resolution having several paragraphs is pending. You feel that it could be dealt with more efficiently if each paragraph could be handled separately. You should obtain the floor and say, "Madam President, I move that the resolution be considered seriatim."

q: A Division of the Assembly can be ordered after a demand by only one member.
If you call for a Division of the Assembly at a meeting of seventy members, this means that the vote must be taken again by raising of hands.
exp: If you call for a Division of the Assembly at a meeting of seventy members, this means that the vote must be taken again by rising.

q: A member can call for a division of the assembly on a motion from the time a voice vote is taken and up until the chair has stated the question on another motion.P
A Division of the Assembly is in order without obtaining the floor or when another member has the floor, and immediately after the vote has been announced.
The motion to call for a Division of the Assembly does not require a second.
When a Division of the Assembly is made by a member of the assembly, the negative vote is taken by the chair first.
exp: When a Division of the Assembly is made by a member of the assembly, the affirmative vote is taken by the chair first.

q: For a Division of the Assembly, debate is allowed if the vote is to be counted and entered in the minutes.
exp: For a Division of the Assembly, debate is not allowed even if the vote is to be counted and entered in the minutes.

q: If a member calls for a Division when a voice vote is obviously a majority, the chair should not allow the cali for a Division because it is dilatory.

The chair has announced the results of a voice vote on an amendment. The result was close. You should say ; Recount" from your seat, without obtaining the floor, to demand that the chair take another vote by rising.
exp: The chair has announced the results of a voice vote on an amendment. The result was close. You should say "Division," "I call for a division," or "I doubt the result of the vote" from your seat, without obtaining the floor, to demand that the chair take another vote by rising.

q: Examples of legal methods of voting other than a voice vote are by ballot, rol! call, and conducting a standing vote.
section: 30. Motions Relating To Methods Of Voting And The Polls

q: A motion to take a roll call vote on a pending motion does not have a higher rank than the motion being voted on.
section: 30. Motions Relating To Methods Of Voting And The Polls
exp: A motion to take a roll call vote on a pending motion takes precedence over the motion being voted on.

q: Incidental motions related to methods of voting are not debatable.
section: 30. Motions Relating To Methods Of Voting And The Polls

q: Incidental motions related to the method of voting and the polls can be applied only to an amendment on which the E assembly is called on to vote.
section: 30. Motions Relating To Methods Of Voting And The Polls
exp: Incidental motions related to the method of voting and the polls can be applied to any motion on which the assembly is called on to vote.

q: All incidental motions related to the methods of voting require a majority vote.
section: 30. Motions Relating To Methods Of Voting And The Polls
exp: Allincidental motions related to the method of voting (except the motion to close the polls which requires a two-thirds vote) require a majority vote.

q: If different methods of voting are suggested, they are treated as filling blanks, and the method that takes the least time s voted on first.k
section: 30. Motions Relating To Methods Of Voting And The Polls
exp: If different methods of voting are suggested, they are treated as filling blanks, and the method that takes the most time is voted on first.

q: Motions relating to nominations may include methods of making nominations and motions to close or open nominations. a
Incidental motions related to nominations must never be seconded.
exp: Incidental motions related to nominations must be seconded.

q: One characteristic of incidental motions related to nominations is that they are not debatable or amendable.
exp: One characteristic of incidental motions related to nominations is that they are not debatable, but are amendable.

q: The minimum affirmative vote necessary to adopt all incidental motions related to nominations is two-thirds.
exp: The minimum affirmative vote necessary to adopt incidental motions related to nominations is a majority, except a motion to close nominations, which requires two-thirds.

q: If suggestions are proposed to nominate from the floor, by a committee, by ballot, or by the chair, they are treated as ng blanks, and nominations by the chair would be voted on first.
The chair usually declares that nominations are closed.
The motion to Postpone Indefinitely cannot be applied to a request to be excused from duty.
section: 32. Request To Be Excused From Duty

q: A motion to Request to be Excused from Duty yields to all privileged motions.
section: 32. Request To Be Excused From Duty

q: A motion to Request to be Excused from Duty is amendable.
section: 32. Request To Be Excused From Duty
exp: The motion to Request to be Excused from Duty is amendable

q: A motion to Request to be Excused from Duty should never be settled by unanimous consent.
section: 32. Request To Be Excused From Duty
exp: The motion to Request to be Excused from Duty is often settied by unanimous consent. 109

q: If a member who has accepted office finds that he or she is unable to perform it, the proper process to use in resigning s to submit a written resignation, and the chair will proceed to have it voted on.
section: 32. Request To Be Excused From Duty

q: If amember has specific duties that are imposed in a society's bylaws and wishes to be excused from one of the duties, the chair can excuse the member from the duty.
section: 32. Request To Be Excused From Duty
exp: If a member has specific duties that are imposed in a society's bylaws and wishes to be excused from one of the duties, the request can be granted by unanimous consent or a motion, unless prevented by the bylaws.

q: If a member who has accepted an office finds that he or she is unable to perform it, the proper process to use in resigning is for the member to submit a written resignation to the secretary or appointing power.
section: 32. Request To Be Excused From Duty

q: Unless the bylaws provide otherwise, when an officer resigns the assembly can fill the vacancy immediately.
section: 32. Request To Be Excused From Duty
exp: Unless the bylaws provide otherwise, when an officer resigns notice must be given before the vacancy can be filled.

q: A Parliamentary Inquiry, Request for Information, and to Withdraw a Motion are examples of motions that members may use to obtain information or to have something done that requires permission of the assembly.
The motion to Call for the Orders of the Day is classified as a type of inquiry or request.
exp: The motion to Call for the Orders of the Day is Not classified as a type of inquiry or request.

q: A Parliamentary Inquiry and a Request for Information require a second.
exp: A Parliamentary Inquiry and a Point of information are not seconded.

q: The motions Request for Information and Parliamentary Inquiry are not debatable or amendable.
A motion for a Parliamentary Information Opinion would be used to obtain the chair's opinion on a matter related to parliamentary procedure as it relates to the pending business.
exp: The motion Parliamentary inquiry would be used to obtain the chairs opinion on a matter related to parliamentary procedure as it relates to the pending business.

q: The chair is obligated to answer ail Parliamentary Inquiry questions except those that are hypothetical in nature.

If a motion to call for the Previous Question is pending, and you are uncertain if this motion is amendable, you could nd out by rising, and without obtaining the floor say, "Madam President, I rise to a parliamentary inquiry."
The chair's reply to a parliamentary inquiry cannot be appealed because the reply is always voted on by the assembly.
exp: The chairs reply to a parliamentary inquiry is not subject to an appeal because the reply is an opinion and not a ruling.

q: A Request for Information is a request directed through the secretary.
exp: A Point of information is a request directed to or through the presiding officer.

q: A Request for Information is a request directed to the chair, or through the chair to another member, for information relevant to parliamentary procedure.
exp: A Point of information is a request directed to the chair, or through the chair to another member, for information relevant to the business at hand, but not concerned with parliamentary procedure.

q: If a main motion is pending, and you have a question that needs to be answered by the maker of the motion, you should rise, and without obtaining the floor say, "Mr. Chairman, ! rise to a request for information."

The chair should ask a member if he or she will yield to a question when another member calls for a request for information because the time consumed in answering the question will be taken out of the member's allowed time.
A motion may be withdrawn by the maker without the consent of anyone before it is stated by the chair.a

You have made a motion "to have a dance next Saturday." Immediately after it has been seconded and before the chair has stated the motion to the assembly, you realize that the club's picnic is the same day. You could cancel your motion by rising, and without obtaining the floor, say, "Mr. President, I withdraw the motion."
If a member suggests a change to the maker of a motion before it is stated by the chair, it must approved by the assembly.
exp: If amember suggests a change to the maker of a motion before it is stated by the chair, it must be approved by the maker of the motion.

q: If a member withdraws his/her second to a modified motion, it is unnecessary for another second because the other member who suggested the changes has essentially seconded it.
To withdraw a motion that has been stated by the chair requires permission of the assembly.
After a motion has been stated by the chair, it belongs to the meeting as a whole. This means the motion may be withdrawn by anyone in the assembly without a vote.
exp: After a motion has been stated by the chair, it belongs to the meeting as a whole. This means the maker of the motion must request the assembly's permission to withdraw the motion.

q: A request for permission to withdraw a motion can be made at any time before voting on the question has begun.
If a Main Motion and the motions to Postpone indefinitely, Limit Debate, and Withdraw are all before the assembly at the same time, the immediately pending motion is to Withdraw.
After a motion has been withdrawn, the same motion cannot be made again at the same meeting.
exp: After a motion has been withdrawn, the same motion can be made again at the same meeting.

q: If you were chair, and a member offered an amendment to a pending motion and the maker of the motion "accepted" t, you would ask for a second and then declare that the amendment is adopted.
exp: If you were chair, and a member offered an amendment to a pending motion and the maker of the motion "accepted" it, you would notify the assembly that the amendment has to be put in the form of a motion before it can be considered.

q: Assume a member wishes to read some pages from a book during debate at a meeting. If another member objects, as chair, you should put the question (take a vote) on granting permission.
The object of the motion to Take from the Table is to make pending again a motion that was postponed.
exp: The object of the motion to Take from the Table is to make pending again a motion that was !aid on the table.

q: The motion to Take from the Table brings a question again before the assembly.
The motion to Take from the Table can be moved when a motion is pending.
exp: The motion to Take from the Table can only be moved when a motion is not pending.

q: The motion to Take from the Table can be made under unfinished or new business and during the same session it is aid on the table.
The motion to Take from the Table is in order at any time.
exp: The motion to Take from the Table is in order when some other business has been transacted since the question was laid on the table.

q: The motion to Take from the Table must be seconded.
The minimum affirmative vote necessary to adopt the motion to Take from the Table is two-thirds and previous notice.
exp: The minimum affirmative vote necessary to adopt the motion to Take from the Table is a majority.

q: A motion that is Taken from the Table cannot be laid on the table again.
exp: A motion that is Taken from the Table can be laid on the table again.

q: A main motion was tabled by an organization that only meets once a year. This group cannot consider this motion at the next meeting by proposing a motion to take it from the table.
A question has been laid on the table and the interrupting, urgent matter has been disposed of. The question can be taken from the table as soon as the interrupting matter has been disposed of.
If the motion to Take from the Table is not proposed within the required time limit, the main motion is automatically placed under "Unfinished Business."
exp: If the motion to Take from the Table is not proposed within the required time limit, the main motion that was laid on the table dies.

q: If a question is taken up on a different day than it was laid on the table, each member may debate the motion one more time.
exp: !f a question is taken up on a different day than it was laid on the table, each member may debate the motion two more times.

q: Suppose you laid a motion "to have a car wash next Saturday" on the table at the beginning of a regular meeting. You could bring it back for consideration at a time later in the same meeting by obtaining the floor and saying, "I move to take from the table the motion related to having a car wash."
The motion to Rescind is a subsidiary motion.
exp: The motion to Rescind is an incidental main motion.

q: The motion to Amend Something Previously Adopted is an incidental main motion.
The motions Annul, Repeal, and Rescind can cancel or countermand a previous action.
A motion that is used to change only a part of a text or to substitute a different version is Amend Something Previously Adopted.
The motion to Rescind can be applied to a secondary amendment which has been adopted.
exp: Normally the motion to Rescind is applied to only main motions which have been adopted.

q: Both of the motions to Rescind and to Amend Something Previously Adopted are debatable, but debate cannot go into the merits of the question that is proposed to be rescinded or amended.49 aa a
exp: Both of the motions to Rescind and to Amend Something Previously Adopted are debatable and debate can go into the merits of the uestion that is proposed to be rescinded or amended.

q: The motion to Rescind can be moved only when no other motion is pending, and it can be applied to most main motions that have been adopted.
The motion to Rescind must be seconded and is debatable and amendable.
The vote needed to pass the motion to Rescind is a majority of the people in attendance.
exp: The vote needed to pass the motion to Rescind is two-thirds of the members in attendance who vote, a majority when notice of intent to make the motion has been given at the previous meeting, or a majority of the entire membership. 110

q: Both the motion to Reconsider and the motion to Rescind must be made by a member who voted on the prevailing side.
exp: The motion to Reconsider must be made by a member who voted on the prevailing side, but the motion to Rescind can be made by any member.

q: If you want to cancel a motion that was adopted at last month's meeting, you should obtain the floor and say, "I move to rescind the motion related to . . . adopted at the meeting last month."
Adoption of the motion to Rescind and Expunge From the Minutes requires a minimum affirmative vote of two-thirds of all the members.
exp: Adoption of the motion to Rescind and Expunge From the Minutes requires a minimum affirmative vote of a majority of the entire membership.

q: When it is necessary to express strong disapproval, a motion to Rescind and Expunge from the Minutes is used. If adopted, the secretary draws a single line through the words in the minutes, writes "Rescinded and Ordered Expunged" with the date and his or her signature across the words, and omits the expunged material from the published minutes.
One purpose of the motion to Discharge a Committee is to officially dismiss a committee after it has made the final report on its task.
exp: One purpose of the motion to Discharge a Committee is to take a matter from a committee's hands before they make a final report on it.

q: The motion to Discharge a Committee must be seconded, takes precedence over nothing, and can be moved only when no other question is pending.
The motion to Discharge a Committee is not undebatable.
exp: The motion to Discharge a Committee is debatable.

q: The motion to Discharge a Committee can apply to any main motion that was referred to a committee which has not made a final report to the assembly.
Debate on the motion to Discharge a Committee cannot go into the merits of the question that was referred to the committee.
exp: Debate on the motion to Discharge a Committee can go into the merits of the question that was referred to the committee.

q: In order to be adopted, the motion to Discharge a Committee requires a vote of the majority of the entire membership, a two-thirds vote of the members present and voting, or a majority vote and previous notice.

Itis appropriate to make the motion to Discharge a Committee if a committee has failed to promptly make a report, if the assembly wants to proceed on the matter without a committee, or if the assembly wants to drop the matter.
When a standing committee is discharged from considering a matter, its existence is discontinued.
exp: When a standing committee is discharged from considering a matter, it continues its existence.

q: When a special committee is discharged from considering a matter, it ceases to exist.

{f your organization is not happy over the progress of the Membership Standing Committee on recruiting new members, and you would like to take it out of their hands, you should obtain the floor and say, "I move that we form a new plan to recruit new committee members."
exp: If your organization is not happy over the progress of the Membership Standing Committee on recruiting new members, and you would ke to take it out of their hands, you should obtain the floor and say, "I move that the Membership Committee be discharged from further consideration of the matter concemed with recruiting new members."

q: The form to use in making the motion to Discharge a Special Committee is (After obtaining the floor), "I move that the committee to which was referred the motion related to . . . be discharged."E 50 a rr
The motion to Reconsider enables a majority of the assembly to bring back for further consideration a motion that has already been voted on.
The purpose of the motion to Reconsider is to withdraw a motion.
exp: The purpose of the motion to Reconsider a vote on a motion is to permit correction of action that was hasty, ill-advised or erroneous.

q: Ata regular meeting of a society, the motion to Reconsider can be made only by the member who voted with the losing side.
exp: Ata regular meeting of a society, the motion to Reconsider can be made only by the member who voted with the prevailing side.

q: The motion to Reconsider can only be moved by a member who voted "Aye" if the motion was adopted, or "No" if the motion was lost.
in a session of one day, the motion to Reconsider may be made on the day after the vote to be reconsidered was taken.
exp: Ina session of one day, the motion to Reconsider must be made on the same day the vote to be reconsidered was taken.

q: The motion to Reconsider cannot be applied to the vote on any motion which has received an affirmative vote dealing with a contract when the party to the contract has been informed of the outcome.
A motion to Reconsider may be made after another member has been assigned the floor, so long as he or she has not begun to speak.
The member who seconds the motion to Reconsider must have voted on the prevailing side.
exp: The member who seconds the motion to Reconsider can vote on either side.

q: The motion to Reconsider is debatable if members debate only in favor of the motion to be reconsidered.
exp: The motion to Reconsider is debatable if the motion that is to be considered is debatable.

q: The motion to Reconsider is not amendabie.
The minimum affirmative vote necessary to adopt a motion to Reconsider at a regular meeting is two-thirds.
exp: The minimum affirmative vote necessary to adopt a motion to Reconsider at a regular meeting is a majority.

q: "The right of each member to debate the motion to Reconsider is separate from the original consideration of the motion proposed to be reconsidered." This means that a member may debate and go into the merits of the question to be considered two more times.
When a member calls up the motion to Reconsider, no second is needed.
Any member who spoke on the prevailing side is entitled to call up the motion to Reconsider if it cannot be taken up when it is made.
exp: The member who made the motion to Reconsider usually calls up the motion to Reconsider if it cannot be taken up when it is made.

q: If reconsideration takes place on a different day in which the vote to be reconsidered was taken, debate ceases for all members on the reconsideration of a question.
exp: If reconsideration takes place ona different day in which the vote to be reconsidered was taken, every member may debate twice in the reconsideration of a question.

q: If there is debate on a motion to reconsider an amendment to a pending main motion, the merits of the amendment may be debated.
If it is desired to reconsider a vote on a primary amendment after the main motion to which it adhered has been disposed of, only the vote on the amendment is reconsidered.
exp: If itis desired to reconsider a vote on a primary amendment after the main motion to which it adhered has been disposed of, the vote on the main question must also be reconsidered.

q: A motion to Reconsider a vote can be made and taken up during a committee meeting at any time after the vote is taken.
The motion to Reconsider, as it relates to special and standing committees, always requires a majority to be adopted.
exp: The motion to Reconsider, as it relates to special and standing committees, requires a majority vote if members who voted with the prevailing side are present or if they have been notified that the reconsideration will be moved.

q: You voted in favor of an adopted motion "to have a picnic next Saturday" and then remembered that you have another engagement on the same day; therefore, you want the motion to be voted on again. You obtain the floor and say, "I move to reconsider the vote on the motion related to the picnic next Saturday. I voted in favor of the motion."
If the maker of the motion to Reconsider does not declare which side he/she voted on, the chair asks the secretary to announce it.
exp: If the maker of the motion to Reconsider does not declare which side he/she voted on, the chair immediately notifies the member to state the fact.

q: If the maker of the motion to Reconsider fails to state which side he/she voted on when the vote was by unanimous consent, the chair should ask if the member was present at the time.
Assume you are the chair at a meeting and a motion to Reconsider a debatable motion is adopted. Your next step would be to put the main motion to a vote.
exp: Assume you are the chair at a meeting and a motion to Reconsider a debatable motion is adopted. Your next step would be to open the main motion to debate.

q: The peculiar nature of the motion to Reconsider and Enter in the Minutes is that it cannot be called up on the day it s made.J
Reconsider and Enter in the Minutes is different from the regular form of Reconsider because it cannot be applied to votes on motions whose object would be defeated by a delay of one day.r
No motion can be renewed during the same session unless the question is proposed by a different member.
exp: No motion can be renewed during the same session unless the question has in some r become different.

q: A main motion cannot be renewed after there has been material progress in business or debate.
The motion to Postpone Indefinitely can be renewed in connection with the same main motion during the same session.
exp: The motion to Postpone indefinitely cannot be renewed in connection with the same main motion during the same session.

q: If the chair rules adversely on a Point of Order, it cannot be raised again during the same meeting unless the chair ndependently brings it up.
exp: Ifthe chair rules adversely on a Point of Order, it cannot be raised again during the same meeting unless an al is made and the chairs decision is reversed.

q: The motion to Adjourn can be renewed after there has been material progress in debate or business.
Motions that seek to obstruct or thwart the will of the assembly are called disruptive motions.
exp: Motions that seek to obstruct or thwart the will of the assembly are called dilatory motions.

q: A demand by a member for a division on every vote even though the results are clear, is an example of a dilatory motion.
Assume a few members constantly called out "Division!" on all voice votes even though the outcome was obviously unanimous. As chair, you should conduct the rising vote each time.
exp: Assume a few members constantly called out "Division!" on all voice votes even though the outcome was obviously unanimous. As chair, you should either not recognize or tule the request out of order because the request for a division is dilatory.

q: An improper motion is one that conflicts with a society's bylaws, the Constitution of the United States, or state or local aws.
If a motion is adopted that conflicts with a motion that has been adopted, it must be implemented.
exp: If a motion is adopted that conflicts with a motion that has been adopted, it is null and void.

q: No motion can be introduced that is outside the object of a society as defined in the bylaws unless the chair permits ts consideration.
exp: No motion can be introduced that is outside the object of a society as defined in the bylaws unless the assembly agrees by a two-thirds vote to consider it.

q: In order that business can be legally transacted in an assembly, a quorum is necessary. A quorum in an assembly is the number of members entitled to vote who are present.
exp: In order that business can be legally transacted in an assembly, a quorum is necessary. A quorum in an assembly is the number of members entitled to vote who must be present.

q: Depending on the organization, the number of members constituting a quorum may vary.

In different organizations, the number of members that constitutes a quorum at a meeting can be determined immediately before roll call by a motion adopted by a majority vote of those members present.
exp: In different organizations, the number of members constituting a quorum is listed in their bylaws.

q: In amass meeting, the quorum is a majority of those persons who indicated they would attend.
exp: In amass meeting, the quorum is the number of persons present at the time.

q: A quorum for a regular meeting of an organization that does not have dues or a listing of actual members consists of the people who attend.
In a body of members such as a convention, and in the absence of any bylaw provision, a quorum is a majority of the registered delegates who are in attendance.
Ina deliberative assembly where the bylaws do not specify a quorum, the quorum is two-thirds of the members present.
exp: In a deliberative assembly where the bylaws do not specify a quorum, the quorum is a majority of all the members.

q: In order to complete their work, volunteer organizations that have an enrolled membership should establish a quorum that is relatively small and less than a majority.
If the quorum provision is struck out in a society's bylaws, a majority of members would automatically become a uorum.
In a committee of the whole, unless the bylaws stipulate differently, the quorum is a majority of the members present at the regular meeting.
exp: In a committee of the whole, unless the bylaws stipulate differently, the quorum is identical as in the assembly.

q: If a quorum is not fixed for boards and committees, a majority of the members must be present to make a quorum.
In the absence of a quorum at an official meeting of a society, any business that is transacted must be carried out.
exp: in the absence of a quorum at an official meeting of a society, the business that may be transacted is null and void.

q: The privileged motion to Fix the Time to Which to Adjoum is in order in the absence of a quorum.
The only action that can legally be taken in the absence of a quorum is to fix the time to which to adjourn.J
exp: The only action that can legally be taken in the absence of a quorum is to fix the time to which to adjourn, to recess or adjourn, and to take measures to obtain a quorum.

q: In the absence of a quorum, a time may be set for an adjourned meeting.
At a meeting without a quorum, emergency matters can be acted on and ratified at a later meeting.
Motions to obtain a quorum are treated as main motions and are adopted by a two-thirds vote.
exp: Motions to obtain a quorum are treated as privileged motions and are adopted by a majority vote.

q: The secretary has the duty to determine if a quorum is present before a meeting is called to order.
exp: The presiding officer has the duty to determine if a quorum is present before a meeting is called to order.

q: In the absence of a quorum, you would take a vote on the motion to Adjourn if you were chair.
If you were chair and noticed that there was not a quorum, you should declare that there is not a quorum.
If there is not a quorum at a meeting, a member should move that the minutes should reflect that a quorum was not present.
exp: If there is not a quorum at a meeting, a member should make a point of order to notify the assembly.

q: If you were chair and noticed that a quorum was no longer present while a member was debating, you should immediately declare the member out of order and adjourn the meeting.
exp: If you were chair and noticed that a quorum was no longer present while a member was debating, you should allow the member to continue speaking. TO
