q: If you were chair and were not in favor of a main motion that just received a tie vote from the assembly, you would not vote and the motion would be lost.
section: 44. Bases For Determining A Voting Result

q: A presiding officer can vote to break a tie, make a tie, or cause or block the reaching of the necessary two-thirds.
section: 44. Bases For Determining A Voting Result

q: If the vote result is 20 in favor and 20 opposed on a main motion, the presiding officer would have to vote in the affirmative in order for the motion to be adopted.
section: 44. Bases For Determining A Voting Result

q: A voting result of 25 in favor and 24 opposed (majority required to adopt) could be affected by a vote of the presiding officer.
section: 44. Bases For Determining A Voting Result
exp: The chair could vote in the negative and thus cause a tie vote and the motion would be rejected.

q: The vote on a main motion is 30 for the affirmative and 29 for the negative. If the chair votes in the negative, the motion s adopted.
section: 44. Bases For Determining A Voting Result
exp: The vote on a main motion is 30 for the affirmative and 29 for the negative. If the chair votes in the negative, the motion is fost.

q: A rising vote on the motion to call for the Previous Question is 59 for the affirmative and 30 for the negative. The chair should abstain in order for the motion to be adopted.
section: 44. Bases For Determining A Voting Result
exp: A rising vote on the motion to call for the Previous Question is 59 for the affirmative and 30 for the negative. The chair should vote in the affirmative in order for the motion to be adopted because it requires a two-thirds vote.

q: If the presiding officer's vote created a tie on an Appeal, the chair's decision is reversed.
section: 44. Bases For Determining A Voting Result
exp: If the presiding officer's vote created a tie on an Appeal, the chairs decision is sustained.

q: The chair can abstain when a motion is voted on.
section: 44. Bases For Determining A Voting Result

q: Members who do not pay their dues and are not formally dropped from the membership roll have no right to vote.
exp: Members who do not pay their dues and are not formally dropped from the membership roll usually have the right to vote if not under disciplinary suspension, except if the bylaws state otherwise.

q: A member should vote in the negative on a motion that wouid result in a direct personal monetary profit.
exp: A member should abstain on the vote on a motion that would result in a direct personal monetary profit.

q: If you were chair, you should allow the vote if a member voted for himself/herself for president of your society.
Members may not explain why they voted in the affirmative or negative because it would be the same as debating.
Members can change their votes on motions without permission from anyone in the assembly up to the time the chair puts the next question.
exp: Members can change their votes on motions without permission from anyone in the assembly up to the time the result is announced.

q: The method of voting by rising is usually used to verify an inconclusive voice vote and on motions requiring a two-thirds vote for adoption.
Voting by a show of hands should be used in large assemblies.
exp: Voting by a show of hands should be used in very small assemblies.

q: The negative vote is always taken first by the chair for a voice vote.
exp: The affirmative vote is always taken first by the chair.

q: If the rising vote that is taken on a voice vote is still inconclusive, the chair can take a rising, counted vote.
A member of a very large assembly who believes a vote must be counted should cail out without rising, "I demand a count!"
exp: A member of a very large assembly who believes a vote must be counted should move that the vote be counted.

q: When counting a rising vote, the negative is always counted first.
exp: When counting a rising vote, the affirmative is always counted first.

q: Voting by ballot is a method of voting which should only be used when expressly ordered by the assembly or prescribed n the bylaws.
Voting by ballot is used when it is desired that members' votes be announced.
exp: Voting by ballot is used when it is desired to keep the members' votes a secret.

q: Voting by ballot is usually followed in the election of officers, admission to membership, and any vote related to charges after a member's trial.
When the bylaws require a vote to be taken by ballot, this requirement may be suspended by a two-thirds vote with previous notice.
exp: When the bylaws require a vote to be taken by ballot, this requirement may not be suspended.

q: Voting by ballot is when members state their vote when their names are called by the presiding officer.
exp: Voting by ballot is when members mark their votes on Slips of paper.

q: Ballot distribution, ballot counting, and reporting the vote are jobs that are usually assigned tellers when voting by ballot.
It is the chair's responsibility to make sure no member votes more than once.
exp: Itis the teller's responsibility to make sure no member votes more than once.

q: The presiding officer, if a member of the assembly, can always vote by ballot with other members.
After the polis are closed on a vote by ballot, the minimum affirmative vote required to reopen them is two-thirds.
exp: After the polls are closed on a vote by ballot, the minimum affirmative vote required to reopen them is a majority.

q: When counting ballots, blank ballots are ignored.
If a teller finds that two filled-out ballots are folded together when recording the votes, they are recorded as legal votes.
exp: Ifa teller finds that two filled-out ballots are folded together when recording the votes, they are recorded as illegal votes.

q: When voting by ballot, if a member leaves one or more of the choices blank on a ballot, the spaces filled should be credited for one legal vote.
When voting by ballot, unintelligible votes are treated as illegal votes.
If illegal votes are cast, the teller should use them only for purposes of computing the majority.
The names of the tellers are not included in a teller's report.
The result of a ballot vote is always declared by the teller making the report.
exp: The result of a ballot vote is always declared by the presiding officer (the chair).

q: An order for a recount on a ballot vote requires a two-thirds vote.
exp: An order for a recount on a ballot vote requires a majority vote.

q: Taking a vote by roll call (also called yeas and nays) places on the record how each member voted.
In the Congress of the United States, the minimum size of the minority that can order a roll call vote is one-third of those present.
exp: In the Congress of the United States, the minimum size of the minority that can order a rolf call vote is one-fifth of those present.

q: In a roll call vote, members who are in favor of adopting a resolution answer "aye," "yes," or "yea."
In a roll call vote, members who are opposed to adopting a resolution answer "reject," "disapprove," or "oppose."
exp: In a roll call vote, members who are opposed to adopting a resolution may only answer "no* or "nay."

q: When taking a vote by roll call, the roll of the assembly is called by the secretary in alphabetical order, with the chair's name called last.
If a member is not ready to vote on a roll call and wishes to be called later, the member answers abstain.
exp: If a member is not ready to vote on a roll call and wishes to be called later, the member answers pass.

q: In roll call voting, a record of how each member voted should be entered in the minutes.
In a roll call vote, members can change their votes if permission is granted by the chair.
exp: In a roll call vote, members can change their votes before the result is announced.

q: A vote by mail, when authorized in the bylaws, is often used to amend bylaws, to elect officers, and when a full membership vote is desired.
Preferential voting is especially useful and fair in an election by mail.
Voting by proxy is a power of attorney, and it controls elections without attendance.
When a member allows another member to vote for him or her, it is called preferential voting.
exp: When a member allows another member to vote for him or her, it is calied proxy voting. 115

q: Strictly speaking, a nomination is a proposal to fill a blank.
It is acceptable to nominate by telephone.
exp: Itis not acceptable to nominate by telephone.

q: Nominations from the floor are sometimes called "oral nominations."
exp: Nominations from the floor are frequently called "gpen nominations."

q: At a mass meeting, the chair is commonly nominated by the vice-president.
exp: Ata mass meeting, the chair is commonly nominated by the person who called the meeting to order.

q: A member need not be recognized when making nominations from the floor.
When nominations for officers are made from the floor, the proper form after a member rises is to say, "I nominate Mr. Smith because . . . (state reasons)"
exp: When nominations for officers are made from the floor, the proper form after a member rises is to say, "I nominate Mr. Smith."

q: tn an organized society, a nominating committee should be elected by the organization or executive board.
All nominees should be contacted by the nominating committee before announcing their nomination.
The time which the nominating committee of an organization reports is determined by the particular organization.
A nominating committee is automatically discharged immediately after the members vote for the nominees.
exp: A nominating committee is automatically discharged when its report is formally presented to the assembly.

q: After the nominating committee has presented its report and before voting for the different offices takes place, the chair must call for further nominations from the floor.

Suppose you are the presiding officer and the nominating committee has submitted a list of nominees to you. After you ask for additional nominations from the floor, and no one responded, you should call for a majority vote to close nominations.
exp: Suppose you are the presiding officer and the nominating committee has submitted a list of nominees to you. After you ask for additional nominations from the floor, and no one responded, you should declare that nominations are closed.

q: The minimum affirmative vote required to close nominations is a majority.
exp: The minimum affirmative vote required to close nominations is two-thirds.

q: The minimum affirmative vote needed to reopen nominations after they are closed is a majority.
exp: a

q: If there is no rule made before an election stating the method of voting in an election, a member may propose an ncidental main motion to determine the method of voting.
The election of officers should take place at the end of the meeting.P
exp: The election of officers should take place early in a meeting.

q: If a member is elected by ballot as both the president and secretary of an organization, the member must take the higher ranking office.
exp: if a member is elected by ballot as both the president and secretary of an organization, the member who was elected to the two offices, present, chooses. a

q: If more than two candidates are nominated for the same office, the candidates all remain on the ballot and the voting continues until one receives a majority vote.
When repeated balloting for an office is necessary, all the names are kept on the ballot.
There has been an election of members of a board. If more than the prescribed number have received a majority vote, those who receive a larger majority fill the place.
A viva voce method of election is especially applicable to mass meetings.
In a viva voce election, candidates are voted on in random order.
exp: In a viva voce election, candidates are voted on in the order they were nominated.

q: When there is only one candidate for the office of president and vice president in a viva voce election, the chair can take a vote on the nominee for president, declare that the nominees are elected without a vote, or take a vote on the candidate for vice president.
When an election is held by a roll call, the secretary should record the vote and remain silent.
exp: When an election is held by a roll call, the secretary should record the vote and repeat it.

q: The qualifications for holding a specific office, how the officers should be elected or appointed, and their term of office should be specified in a society's bylaws if they are different from those stated in the parliamentary authority.
The official duties of the officers of a society, if they are different to those stated in the parliamentary authority, are determined by the society's officers.
exp: The official duties of the officers of a society, if they are different to those stated in the parliamentary authority are determined by the society's bylaws.

q: An officer who has served ten percent of a term is considered to have served a full term.
exp: An officer who has served more than half of a term is considered to have served a full term.

q: Generally, an officer's term begins the following January after being elected.
exp: Generally, an officer's term begins as soon as elected.

q: When no special title has been assigned, the presiding officer of an assembly is generally called the chair or president.
In a mass meeting, the presiding officer is known as the moderator.
exp: In amass meeting, the presiding officer is known as the chair.

q: The term used both for the person who is presiding and the presiding officer's station is the bench.
exp: The term used both for the person who is presiding and the presiding officer's station is the chair.

q: The presiding officer of a large assembly should be chosen chiefly on an ability to preside.
Enforcing the rules of debate and announcing the proper sequence of business are two duties of the presiding officer of an assembly.
One of the duties of a presiding officer of an assembly is to restrain business.
exp: One of the duties of a presiding officer of an assembly is to expedite business.

q: At any meeting, the presiding officer should have a copy of the bylaws of the organization, a copy of the parliamentary authority of the organization, and a list of the standing and special committees and the members.
In a large assembly, the presiding officer should stand when calling the meeting to order, putting a question to a vote, and explaining reasons for a ruling on a point of order.
When a member is speaking in debate, the presiding officer should remain standing.
exp: When a member is speaking in debate, the presiding officer should be seated.

q: The presiding officer should not hesitate to put the question on a motion that elects officers even when he/she is ncluded.
The second vice-president precedes the first vice-president in the right to preside.
exp: The president-elect precedes the first vice-president in the right to preside. The vice-president presides in the piace of the president if an organization does not have a president-elect.

q: If the presiding officer has to vacate the chair during a meeting and a vice-president is not available, the chair, with the approval of the assembly, can appoint a chair pre term.
exp: If the presiding officer has to vacate the chair during a meeting and a vice-president is not available, the chair, with the approval of the assembly, can appoint a chair pro tem.

q: If neither the president or vice-president is present, a meeting should be called to order by the parliamentarian.
exp: If neither the president or vice-president is present, a meeting should be called to order by the secretary..

q: In the absence of a society's president and vice-president, a chair pro tem should be elected.
The office of an elected chair pro tem can be terminated by the entrance of the vice-president, the election of another chair pro tem, or the arrival of the president.
An effective presiding officer should know more parliamentary procedure than any other member, but should never be more technical than necessary.
A president who is an ex-officio member of a committee may not vote on issues at meetings.
exp: A president who is an ex-officio member of a committee has the same rights as other members.

q: When an organization elects its president one entire term in advance, the person chosen is called the president pro tempore.
exp: When an organization elects its president one entire term in advance, the person chosen is called the president-elect.

q: A member who has completed a full term as president-elect will become the organization's vice-president.
exp: A member who has completed a full term as president-elect will become the organization's president.

q: The officer who takes the place of an absent president is the vice-president.
Unless it will be confusing, the vice-president should be addressed as "Mr. or Madam President" when presiding.
If the president of an organization resigns, the third vice-president becomes the first vice-president.
exp: If the president of an organization resigns, the second vice-president becomes the first vice-president.

q: The secretary of a society must be proficient in serving as the recording officer of the assembly and the custodian of the records.
Another name for the secretary is the transcribing secretary.
exp: Another name for the secretary is the clerk, recording secretary, or scribe.

q: A secretary should not preside for an entire meeting upon the absence of the president.
exp: The secretary should call the meeting to order and preside until the election of chair pro tem.

q: The secretary should not modify the bylaws to compose an order of business for all meetings.
If the secretary is absent at a regular meeting, the vice-president should assume the duties.
exp: If the secretary is absent at a regular meeting, a secretary pro tem should be elected.

q: Correspondence of an official nature is normally read by the vice-president.
exp: Correspondence of an official nature is normally read by the recording secretary.

q: Any interested person has the right to examine the minutes of a society if requested at a reasonable time and place.
exp: Any member has the right to examine the minutes of a society if requested at a reasonable time and place.

q: In larger societies, a corresponding secretary has the duty of issuing notices of meetings.
The name of the officer who is entrusted with the custody of an organization's funds is the vice-president.
exp: The name of the officer who is entrusted with the custody of an organization's funds is the treasurer.

q: The specific duties of the treasurer are varied and are dependent on the size and complexity of the organization.

In some organizations, in addition to the treasurer, a financial secretary performs the duty of billing members for their dues, receiving members' dues, and maintaining a ledger of each member's account.
The librarian is responsible to write a narrative account of the society's activities.
exp: The historian is responsible to write a narrative account of the society's activities.

q: Directors, or trustees, or managers are names given to members who may serve as members of an executive board.
The officer who serves as a custodian of objects of value (except library materials) is called the security master.
exp: The officer who serves as a custodian of objects of value (except library materials) is called the curator.

q: A Sergeani-at-arms is sometimes called a Curator.
exp: A sergeant-at-arms is sometimes called a warden or warrant officer.

q: The name of the officer who assists the chair in preserving order and sometimes serves notices of fines is the staff sergeant.
exp: The name of the officer who assists the chair in preserving order and sometimes serves notices of fines is the sergeant-at-arms.

q: If a meeting is restricted to members only, the doorkeeper can check credentials as people arrive at a meeting.
Directors should always be appointed by the president.[
exp: Directors should always be elected.

q: An honorary office is a complimentary title and may be granted to members and nonmembers.
When an individual is conferred an honorary office or membership in an organization, it must be renewed each year.
exp: When an individual is conferred an honorary office or membership in an organization, it is perpetual unless rescinded or qualified by the bylaws.

q: Honorary officers and honorary members of an organization normally may not make motions and vote.
Honorary presidents and vice-presidents should sit in the front row with the assembly.
exp: Honorary presidents and vice-presidents should sit on the platform.

q: The executive secretary supervises the central office and acts under the immediate direction of the board and executive committee.
Some of the duties of an executive secretary (or director) in a national organization that can be completed without the approval of the board are to hire staff and determine their salaries.
exp: Normally the only duty of an executive secretary (or director) in a national organization that can be completed without the approval of the board is to conduct day-to-day regular business.

q: The consultant who advises officers, committees, and members on matters concerning parliamentary procedure is called the parliamentarian.
A parliamentarian for an organization should be appointed by the vice-president.J
exp: A parliamentarian for an organization should be appointed by the president.

q: The presiding officer should confer with the parliamentarian before a meeting begins.P
During a meeting, the work of the parliamentarian may include rising to points of order whenever a breach of order is made by a member.
exp: During a meeting, the work of the parliamentarian should be limited to giving advice to the chair and members and serving as a consultant.

q: At a regular meeting, the parliamentarian should be seated in an inconspicuous place.
exp: At a regular meeting, the parliamentarian should be seated next to the chair.

q: After a parliamentarian declares a position on a point, the chair must follow the advice given.
exp: After a parliamentarian deciares a position on a point, the chair may disregard the advice given.

q: The parliamentarian can only vote when the vote is by ballot.
The minutes of a meeting of legislative bodies sometimes are called the record.
exp: The minutes of a meeting of legislative bodies sometimes are called the journal.

q: In an ordinary society, the minutes should contain a record of what was done at a meeting.
The minutes of a meeting should indicate if the minutes of the previous meeting were read and approved and contain all the main motions and all notices of motions.
The first paragraph of the minutes of a reguiar meeting should contain the fact that the organization's regular vice- president and treasurer were in attendance.
exp: The first paragraph of the minutes of a regular meeting should contain the fact that the organization's regular president and secretary were n attendance.

q: In writing minutes, a proficient secretary will re-word motions that are acted upon.
exp: In writing minutes, a proficient secretary will use the exact wording of motions that are acted upon.

q: If a secondary motion is withdrawn, the motion still must appear in the minutes.
exp: If a secondary motion is withdrawn, the motion does not appear in the minutes.

q: The last paragraph of the minutes should state the hour of adjournment.r
The number of votes on each side should be entered in the minutes on a voice vote.
exp: The number of votes on each side should be entered in the minutes when a count is ordered or the vote is by ballot.

q: The name of the seconder of a motion should be included in the minutes of a meeting.
exp: The name of the seconder of a motion should generally not be included in the minutes of a meeting.

q: The proceedings of the committee of the whole should not be entered in the minutes.

When a question is considered informally, the information that should be included in the minutes is the exact wording of adopted main motions, the member who made the motion and the disposition of the motion.
When the assembly orders a committee report "to be entered in the minutes," this means the secretary may write an nterpretation of the report in the minutes.
exp: When the assembly orders a committee report "to be entered in the minutes," this means the secretary must copy the entire report into the minutes.

q: A summary of the guest speaker's remarks should not be included in the minutes.
The minutes of a meeting should be signed only by the president.
exp: The minutes of a meeting should be signed by the secretary, and if the assembly wishes, by the president.

q: When the secretary signs the minutes, the words Respectfully Submitted should always be used.
exp: When the secretary signs the minutes, the words Aespectfully Submitted should not be included.

q: Normally, in most organizations, the minutes of each meeting are read and approved at the beginning of the next regular meeting after the meeting is called to order and opening ceremonies are completed.
If a motion is referred to a committee, the committee members' names that are appointed by the chair must be included n the minutes.
An adjourned meeting of an ordinary society has its minutes approved at the next regular or adjourned meeting (whichever comes first).
Any corrections and the approval of the minutes are normally accomplished by unanimous consent of the assembly.
The reading of the minutes can be "dispensed with" by a majority vote and without debate. This means that the minutes need not be read at any time.
exp: The reading of the minutes can be "dispensed with" by a majority vote and without debate. This means that the minutes must still be read at a later time.

q: If a draft of the minutes are sent to all members in advance, they are not read to the assembly unless requested.
In conventions lasting five days, the minutes of the previous day's meetings are usually read and approved at the end of each day's business.
exp: In conventions tasting five days, the minutes of the previous day's meetings are usually read and approved at the beginning of each day's business.

q: When minutes have been approved by the assembly, the secretary writes "Approved" with the date and initials it below them.
If an error is found in the minutes several years after approval, they can be corrected by means of the motion to Reconsider and alter.
exp: If an error is found in the minutes several years after approval, they can be corrected by means of the motion to Amend Something Previously Adopted.

q: Corrections to minutes may be made by the society at any time a mistake is discovered.
When "minutes" are to be published, they contain only a list of the members who spoke pro and con on every question.
exp: When "minutes" are to be published, they contain (in addition to the regular information) a list of the members who spoke pro and con on every question, an abstract of each speech, and committee reports exactly as they were submitted to the secretary.

q: When using the standard order of business, the reports of the officers are presented at the discretion of the secretary.
exp: When using the standard order of business, the reports of the officers are presented immediately after the reading and approval of the minutes.

q: Any member except the reporting officer may propose a motion to implement a report made by an officer.
After the "Treasurer's report" is made at a regular meeting, it requires no action from the assembly.
The annual treasurer's report should always be audited.
The "Treasurer's report" for a regular meeting should always contain dates of each receipt and dates of each disbursement.
exp: The "Treasurer's report" for a regular meeting may contain only a verbal statement of the cash balance on hand.

q: In ordinary societies, the financial reports are audited by elected members known as "accountants."
exp: In ordinary societies, the financial reports are audited by elected members known as "trustees."

q: The adoption of the auditor's report has the effect of relieving the treasurer of all responsibilities.
exp: The adoption of the auditor's report has the effect of relieving the treasurer of responsibility for the period covered by the report except for i raud. TO BO

q: If an organization wishes a historical account to be part of the official history of the society, it must be formally adopted by the assembly after a presentation by the historian.
When a board is empowered by its bylaws to act for a society between regular meetings, it is called an Ex-officio board.
exp: When a board is empowered by its bylaws to act for a society between regular meetings, it is called an executive board.

q: Another name for the "executive board" is board of directors.
If a society desires an executive board, the bylaws should indicate the number of board members, their duties and powers, how they are to be determined, and make provisions for meetings.
In organizations that meet monthly or more often, a board is given all the power.
exp: In organizations that meet monthly or more often, a board is not given so much power.

q: The society's assembly can countermand any action of the executive board except those matters placed by the bylaws exclusively under the control of the board.
An ex-officio member of a board must be a member of the society.
exp: An ex-officio member of a board may be a nonmember of the society.

q: A govermor of a state who is an ex-officio board member of a private hospital should be counted in determining a uorum.
exp: A governor of a state who is an ex-officio board member of a private hospital should not be counted in determining a quorum.

q: In ordinary societies having executive boards, the president and secretary of the society may serve in the same capacity within the board.
A board generally cannot delegate its authority.

In an organization where the board is large or its members must travel from a distance to meet, the bylaws can establish a "board within a board" called an ex-officio committee.14. Business is transacted in a large board by the same rules of parliamentary law as in any other deliberative assembly.
exp: In an organization where the board is large or its members must travel! from a distance to meet, the bylaws can establish a "board within a board" called an executive committee.

q: A board can transact business if every board member has been notified.
exp: A board can transact business if every board member has been notified, a quorum is present, and it is a regular or properly called meeting.

q: A quorum of a board, if not stated differently in the bylaws, is more than half the members.
Personal board member approval of a proposed emergency action obtained separately by telephone has the same effect as approval at a regular board meeting.
exp: Personal board member approval of a proposed action obtained separately by telephone must be ratified at the next reguiar board meeting.

q: One way to allow the minutes of board proceedings to be accessible to others is to grant special permission. P
The minutes of a board meeting may be made accessible for inspection to members of the society by a two-thirds vote of the society or by previous notice and a majority vote of the assembly.
Rules of debate at small board meetings of about twelve or less members provide that members can speak three times on each debatable motion.
exp: Rules of debate at small board meetings of about twelve or less members provide that members can speak as often as desired on each debatable motion.

q: In a small board meeting, the chair still should rise while putting motions to a vote.
exp: Ina small board meeting, the chair does not need to rise while putting motions to a vote.

q: In a small board meeting of about a dozen members or less, the chair can make motions.
If there are periodic changes in a board's membership, all unfinished business that existed falls to the ground, and if the board appoints its standing committees, new ones are chosen.
During debate in small board meetings, the chair must relinquish the chair to speak.
exp: During debate in small board meetings, the chair can speak without rising or leaving the chair.

q: A committee can be directed to take action on specific matters and may consist of one person.
One primary difference between a board and a committee is that the board has more authority to act independently or the assembly.
When a committee is appointed "with power," this means that the committee has permission from the president to add more members to the committee and to decide all related matters in the future.
exp: When a committee is appointed "with power," the committee has permission to take the necessary steps to carry out its instructions.

q: A committee that has a continuing existence and is named in the society's bylaws it is called a standard committee.
exp: A committee that has a continuing existence and is named in the society's bylaws is called a slanding committee.

q: Unless the bylaws state otherwise, members of standing committees usually serve until their successors are chosen or the same length of term as the officers of the organization.
If certain standing committees are listed in the bylaws, no other standing committees can be established unless the president grants permission.
exp: If certain standing committees are listed in the bylaws, no other standing committees can be established unless the bylaws are amended.

q: A standing committee of an organization reports to the president.
exp: A standing committee of an organization usually reports to the assembly.

q: Special, select, and ad hoc committees are the same.
A committee that is appointed to carry out a specific task and ceases to exist when it has made a final report to the assembly is called a special, select, or ad hoc committee.
After a special committee has made its final report to the assembly, it is listed in the bylaws and handles all related matters as a standing committee.
exp: After a "special committee* has made its final report to the assembly, it ceases to exist.

q: The method of appointing assembly members to a special committee is usually specified in the motion that establishes the committee.
A vacancy occurring in a committee is filled by the committee itself.
exp: A vacancy occurring in a committee is filled by the appointing power (usually the chair).

q: If a standing committee has extensive powers, it is usually chosen in an election by viva voce.
exp: Ifa standing committee has extensive powers, it is usually chosen in an election by ballot.

q: In large assemblies, special committees are generally appointed by the secretary.
exp: in large assemblies, special committees are generally appointed by the chair.

q: In general practice, when a committee is nominated by the chair, the committee chair is the last member the chair names to the committee.
exp: In general practice, when a committee is nominated by the chair, the committee chair is the first member the chair names to the committee.

q: Some society's bylaws state that the president "shall appoint all committees."
A standing committee can appoint subcommittees who then are accountable to and report to the assembly.
exp: A standing committee can appoint subcommittees who are then accountable to and report to the standing committee.

q: When a special committee is designated to execute an order of the assembly, it should include only members who are neither in favor nor approve of the action.74 a 20. Some of the duties of the secretary of a society when a committee is appointed are to notify all persons who are appointed, furnish a list of all members to the committee chair, and provide copies of all papers, motions, or matters referred to it.
exp: Whena special committee is designated to execute an order of the assembly, it should include only members who approve that the motion be carried out. ee

q: The minimum number of committee members that can call a meeting if the chair does not is three.
exp: The minimum number of committee members that can cail a meeting if the chair does not is two.

q: If an assembly has no bylaw provision or rule about the quorum of a committee, the quorum of a standing committee s all the members of the committee.
exp: If an assembly has no bylaw provision or rule about the quorum of a committee, the quorum of a standing committee is a majority of the committee members

q: A brief memorandum for committee use is adequate for the minutes of a large committee meeting.
In relatively small standing and special committees, the chair should not debate motions.
exp: In relatively small standing and special committees, the chair may debate motions.

q: Committees of organized societies normally operate under the parliamentary authority adopted by the society.
When members of a society appear before a committee to present their views on a subject studied by the committee, the meeting is called a mass meeting.
exp: When members of a society appear before a committee to present their views on a subject studied by the committee, the meeting is called a hearing.

q: Only members of the committee have the right to be present during deliberation of a committee when it is a hearing.
When a special committee has completed the business it was assigned, a motion can be made for the committee to rise," which means that the committee is adjourned sine die.
The motion to "rise" is used in standing committees.
exp: The motion to "rise" is never used in standing committees.

q: Members of standing committees generally continue their duties until they make a report.
exp: Members of standing committees generally continue their duties until new officers of the society replace them.

q: Standing committees are generally required to report at least once a year at the annual meeting.
The form for a detailed report by a committee should consist of four parts, and recommendations are covered last.
The committee co-chair, any other member of the committee, or the secretary of the committee is allowed to make a report for a board if the chair of the board is also the presiding officer.
The presenter of a committee report is usually the committee secretary.
exp: The presenter of a committee report is usually the committee chair.

q: When an assembly receives a committee report, this means that the assembly adopts a report after it is read.
exp: When an assembly receives a committee report, the assembly hears the report that is read.

q: Acommittee report is read which contains certain recommendations. The appropriate motion at the end of the report made by the reporting committee member would be to implement the recommendations.
A motion made to the assembly after a committee report requires a second.
exp: A motion made to the assembly after a committee report requires no second if the committee consists of more than one person.

q: A motion arising out of a report of an officer, board, or committee is taken up under new business.
exp: A motion arising out of a report of an officer, board, or committee is taken up immediately after the report is read.

q: When a member of the assembly makes a motion to implement the recommendations of a report rather than the person presenting the report, the motion should be seconded.
A motion "to adopt the report" of a committee has the effect of endorsing every word of the report.
When an assembly acts favorably toward a committee report, it is usually best to use the words agree to.
exp: When an assembly acts favorably toward a committee report, it is usually best to use the word adopt.

q: If a motion "to accept" a committee report is adopted, it implies that the assembly has agreed to hear the report and vote on it.
exp: If a motion "to accept" a committee report is adopted, it implies that the assembly has endorsed the entire report.

q: A board report is usually signed by every member of the board.
exp: A board report is usually signed by the president and secretary of the board.

q: A written committee report is usually not addressed or dated, and should begin with the identification of the committee that submitted it.
The wording "The committee has studied . . . and we have decided that. . . " is not correct for the opening statement of a special committee report.
If a written committee report is very important, it should be signed by the concurring committee members.
"Approved" should be written after the signature of the chair if a committee authorizes its chair to sign a report.
exp: "Chair" shouid be written after the signature of the chair if a committee authorizes its chair to sign a report.

q: If the order of business does not make a provision for a committee report that one member does not want to be received, and a member still wishes to make the report, as chair, you should put the question to the assembly.
After a report from a standing committee concludes by making a recommendation to adopt a resolution, the resolution can be adopted by the assembly by the reporting member first proposing a motion.
If a motion is referred to a committee while the motion to postpone it indefinitely is immediately pending, the motion to Postpone indefinitely is taken up by the assembly when the committee reports.
exp: Ifa motion is referred to a committee while the motion to postpone it indefinitely is immediately pending, the motion to Postpone indefinitely s not taken up by the assembly when the committee reports.

q: A single motion can be made to adopt all the amendments if a report that includes amendments recommended by a committee is made.
The chair takes a vote on each recommendation after it is read and opened for debate on a committee's recommendation of several amendments.
After a committee makes a report that contains only details of work completed, it is usually voted on by the assembly.
exp: After a committee makes a report that contains only details of work completed, it is filed and no action should be taken on it.

q: The principal committees that perform parliamentary functions in the organization of a convention are the Credentials Committee, the Committee on Standing Rules, and the Program Committee.
The formal presentation of the views of committee members who do not agree with the committee report is called a protesting report."
exp: The formal presentation of the views of committee members who do not agree with the committee report is called a "minority report."

q: The report adopted by a majority in a committee is referred to as "the majority report."
exp: The report adopted by a majority in a committee is referred to as "the committee report."

q: The formal presentation of a "minority report" is a right that must be allowed without permission of the assembly.
exp: The formal presentation of a "minority report" is a privilege that the assembly may grant.

q: If the minority committee report concludes with a proposed resolution, the minority can recommend amendment or rejection of the resolution or adoption of some other suitable motion.
If you were the chair and called for a minority report and a member of the assembly objects, you should not allow the report.
exp: If you were the chair and called for a minority report and a member of the assembly objects, you should have the assembly vote on the request.

q: A mass meeting is an alternate form of the committee of the whole.
section: 52. Committee Of The Whole And Its Alternate Forms
exp: A guasi committee of the whole and informal consideration are alternate forms of the committee of the whole.

q: The committee of the whole, quasi committee of the whole, and informal consideration all allow members to debate any main motion or amendment a maximum of three times.
section: 52. Committee Of The Whole And Its Alternate Forms
exp: The committee of the whole, quasi committee of the whole, and informal consideration all allow members to debate any main motion or amendment as often as they are able to get the floor.

q: A Committee of the whole is suited for large assemblies.
section: 52. Committee Of The Whole And Its Alternate Forms

q: The chair of a committee of the whole is elected.
section: 52. Committee Of The Whole And Its Alternate Forms
exp: The chair of a committee of the whole is appointed.

q: The president normally acts as chair for a committee of the whole.
section: 52. Committee Of The Whole And Its Alternate Forms
exp: The president normally acts as chair for a quasi committee of the whole. The chair of the committee of the whole is appointed.

q: A quasi committee of the whole is suited for groups of fifty to one-hundred members.
section: 52. Committee Of The Whole And Its Alternate Forms

q: Informal consideration is suitable for small meetings of an ordinary society.
section: 52. Committee Of The Whole And Its Alternate Forms

q: In a quasi committee of the whole, the president of a society normally acts as the chair.
section: 52. Committee Of The Whole And Its Alternate Forms

q: During the informal consideration of a motion, members can only debate amendments one time.
section: 52. Committee Of The Whole And Its Alternate Forms
exp: During the informal consideration of a motion, members can debate amendments as many times as they can get the floor.

q: During informal debate of a motion at a meeting, the "informal" aspect allows debating without recognition from the chair.
section: 52. Committee Of The Whole And Its Alternate Forms
exp: During informal debate of a motion at a meeting, the "informal" aspect removes the number of times members can debate.

q: In a committee of the whole, the chair of the committee is appointed, it is technically not "the assembly," and the committee adopts a report to be made to the assembly.
section: 52. Committee Of The Whole And Its Alternate Forms

q: To have the assembly go into a committee of the whole, a member would obtain the floor and state, "I move to go into a committee of the whole and to consider the pending question."
section: 52. Committee Of The Whole And Its Alternate Forms

q: The vice-president is generally appointed by the presiding officer to assume the chair if a motion to refer to a committee of the whole is adopted.
section: 52. Committee Of The Whole And Its Alternate Forms

q: The proceedings of a committee of the whole are entered into the minutes of the assembly.
section: 52. Committee Of The Whole And Its Alternate Forms
exp: The proceedings of a committee of the whole are Not entered into the minutes of the assembly.

q: The actual motion of the referral to a committee of the whole, the report, and the assembly's action on the report should all be included in the minutes of a regular meeting regarding a committee of the whole.
section: 52. Committee Of The Whole And Its Alternate Forms

q: A committee of the whole can propose amendments and adopt them for the regular assembly.
section: 52. Committee Of The Whole And Its Alternate Forms
exp: A committee of the whole can propose amendments and report them as recommendations to the assembly.

q: The motion to Appeal from the Decision of the Chair is not in order in committee of the whole.
section: 52. Committee Of The Whole And Its Alternate Forms
exp: The motion to Appeal from the Decision of the Chair is in order in a committee of the whole.

q: Subcommittees cannot be appointed and motions to adjourn or to recess cannot be proposed when the assembly is n a committee of the whole.
section: 52. Committee Of The Whole And Its Alternate Forms

q: A committee of the whole can refer a matter to another special committee.
section: 52. Committee Of The Whole And Its Alternate Forms
exp: A committee of the whole cannot refer a matter to another special committee.

q: Unless prescribed in the bylaws, the quorum for a committee of the whole is established by the committee as the first new business.
section: 52. Committee Of The Whole And Its Alternate Forms
exp: Unless prescribed in the bylaws, the quorum for a committee of the whole is the same as that of the assembly.

q: If a committee of the whole lacks a quorum at any time, it must first rise and report the fact to the assembly.
section: 52. Committee Of The Whole And Its Alternate Forms

q: When the assembly goes into a quasi committee of the whole, the vice-president presides throughout its proceedings.
section: 52. Committee Of The Whole And Its Alternate Forms
exp: When the assembly goes into a quasi committee of the whole, the presiding officer remains in the chair throughout its proceedings.

q: If the motion below was proposed, the chair should ask for a second, ask for debate, and then take a vote on the a motion.MEMBER (After obtaining the floor):-"I move that the resolution be considered in quasi committee of the whole."
section: 52. Committee Of The Whole And Its Alternate Forms

q: In a quasi committee of the whole, each member is allowed to debate on motions three times.
section: 52. Committee Of The Whole And Its Alternate Forms
exp: In a quasi committee of the whole, each member is allowed to debate on motions an unlimited number of times.

q: If an assembly considers a question informally, this means that there is no limit on the number of times members can speak in debate on main questions and their amendments.
section: 52. Committee Of The Whole And Its Alternate Forms

q: The proceedings should be recorded in the minutes when a meeting is under informal consideration.
section: 52. Committee Of The Whole And Its Alternate Forms

q: When a question is considered informally, as soon as it is disposed of the informal consideration is carried to the next uestion automatically.
section: 52. Committee Of The Whole And Its Alternate Forms
exp: When a question is considered informally, as saon as it is disposed of, the informal consideration ceases automatically. 119

q: A mass meeting, as understood in parliamentary law, is a meeting of ail the clubs in an organization.
exp: A mass meeting, as understood in parliamentary law, is a meeting of an unorganized group called to take appropriate action on a specific problem. 7 Fe

q: Amass meeting would not occur in an organized society.
One characteristic of a mass meeting is that they are called to only take action on a specific problem.
One characteristic of a mass meeting is that the sponsors may never limit the right of attendance.
exp: One feature of a mass meeting is that the sponsors may limit the right of attendance to in sympathy with the purpose of the meeting.

q: The person chosen as chair for a mass meeting should know many of the people who attend, have a thorough understanding of the object of the meeting, and be skilled as a presiding officer.
Ifamass meeting was attended by several people who were not invited, the chair should welcome them and invite them to participate.
exp: If amass meeting was attended by several people who were not invited, the chair can ask them to leave.

q: In amass meeting, a standard parliamentary authority can be adopted by a majority vote on a motion from a member.
exp: a_i

q: In a mass meeting, the officers that are generally elected are a chair and vice-president.
exp: In a mass meeting, the officers that are generally elected are a chair and secretary.

q: The people who attend may change the original purpose of the mass meeting.
exp: The people who attend may not change the original purpose of the mass meeting.

q: A chair and secretary of a mass meeting are elected by the assembly after the first meeting is called to order. Y
The name chosen by the sponsors should be placed in nomination first for each office in the election of officers for a mass meeting.
After the chair is elected by a voice vote in a mass meeting, the next step for the chair is to conduct an election or a parliamentarian.
exp: After the chair is elected by a voice vote in a mass meeting, the next step for the chair is to conduct an election for a secretary.

q: After elections are completed at a mass meeting, the officer who reads the call of the meeting is the president.
exp: After elections are completed at a mass meeting, the officer who reads the call of the meeting is the secretary.

q: If a mass meeting was organized to oppose a new garbage dump in your neighborhood, and a member proposed a motion "to endorse the garbage dump location in the neighborhood," the chair should cail the motion out of order.
exp: Any motion that is contrary to the purpose of the mass meeting is out of order.

q: In a mass meeting, assembly members can generally speak no longer than thirty minutes at a time.
exp: In a mass meeting, assembly members can generally speak no longer than ten minutes at a time.

q: If resolutions have not been written before a mass meeting, a committee should be designated at the meeting to draft them.
All committees at a mass meeting should be appointed by the people attending.
exp: It is advisable to have all committees at a mass meeting appointed by the chair.

q: Unless a time has been set for another meeting at a mass meeting, a motion to adjourn should not be made while business is pending.
At a mass meeting, unless a time has been set for another meeting, the adoption of the motion to Adjourn dissolves a the assembly.
If the members at a mass meeting are trying to organize a permanent society and need to have more meetings, the presiding officer elected at the first meeting is designated as the chair tro pem.
exp: Ifthe members at a mass meeting are trying to organize a permanent society and need to have more meetings, the presiding officer elected at the first meeting is designated as chair pro tem.

q: The first business of a meeting to organize a permanent society is to elect a permanent chair.
exp: The first business of a meeting to organize a permanent society is to nominate a chair pro tem.

q: After a resolution to organize a society is adopted, the next step is usually the introduction and adoption of a motion that the secretary draft bylaws.
exp: After a resolution to organize a society is adopted, the next step is usually the introduction and adoption of a motion that a committee be appointed by the chair to draft bylaws.

q: The first draft of a newly organized society's bylaws are written by a chair pro tem and secretary pro tem.
exp: The first draft of a newly organized society's bylaws is written by a committee.

q: After a committee has been selected to draft bylaws to form a permanent society, the next step should be the presentation and adoption of a motion to fix the date, hour, and place of the next meeting.
The committee selected to draft bylaws for an incorporated society should consult a professional parliamentarian and confer with an attorney.
The first item of business at the second organizational meeting in organizing a society is the reading and approval of the minutes of the first meeting.

If there is not a proposal for a corporate charter, the report of the bylaws committee are received at the second organizational meeting of a permanent society immediately after the president calls the meeting to order.
exp: If there is not a proposal for a corporate charter, the report of the bylaws committee are received at the second organizational meeting of a permanent society immediately after the minutes are approved.

q: Members of a new society who sign a permanent record sheet that will be filed with the original papers of the organization are called "chapter members."
exp: Members of a new society who sign a permanent record sheet that will be filed with the original papers of the organization are called charter members."

q: In organizing a permanent society, after the bylaws are adopted and a recess is taken to enroll members, the election of permanent officers is the next immediate business.
When two existing societies wish to merge, one of the two continues, while the other ceases to exist.
section: 55. Merger, Consolidation, And Dissolution Of Societies

q: When two or more organizations merge or consolidate, the resulting organization must use parts of each group's name n the new name.
section: 55. Merger, Consolidation, And Dissolution Of Societies
exp: When two or more organizations merge or consolidate, the resulting organization may be given a new name.

q: If an unincorporated society wishes to discontinue its existence, it should adopt a motion to disband.
section: 55. Merger, Consolidation, And Dissolution Of Societies
exp: !f an unincorporated society wishes to cease its existence, it should adopt a resolution to rescind its byiaws.

q: The vote required to adopt a resolution to dissolve an unincorporated society is the same as the vote and notice required to amend the bylaws.80 BYLAWS
section: 55. Merger, Consolidation, And Dissolution Of Societies

q: A committee to draft proposed bylaws is normally designated when the society is being formed at the second organizational meeting.
exp: A committee to draft proposed bylaws is normally designated when the society is being formed at the first organizational meeting.

q: A committee to draw up proposed bylaws should be large.
In writing bylaws, the committee should write each sentence so it would be impossible to quote them out of context.
If the existing bylaws of an organization require a minimum three-fourths affirmative vote to amend, a revision of the bylaws would require a minimum affirmative vote of two-thirds.
exp: If the existing bylaws of an organization require a minimum three-fourths affirmative vote to amend, a revision of the bylaws would require a minimum affirmative vote of three-fourths.

q: Bylaws that bring a society into being are adopted by a two-thirds vote.
exp: Bylaws that bring a society into being are adopted by a majority vote.

q: Articles of bylaws are commonly designated with Roman numerals.
The first article in an unincorporated society's bylaws lists the society's members.
exp: The first article in an unincorporated society's bylaws lists the society's name.

q: In forming a new, unincorporated society, Article Il: Object of the bylaws should be general.
Usuatly the article on members in the bylaws covers classes of members, qualifications or eligibility of members, and the required fees and dues and the dates that dues must be paid.
An article listing the officers' names are not included in the bylaws.
The bylaws should provide that the president be listed last in the bylaw article listing the officers.
exp: The bylaws should provide that the president should be listed first in the bylaw article listing the officers.

q: The bylaw article dealing with elections should provide for methods of nominating officers.
exp: The bylaw article dealing with officers should provide for methods of nominating officers.

q: How officers are elected, their length of term, and the method of nominating should all be included in Article IV: Officers.
An officer must serve half of the term before it is considered a full term.
exp: An officer must serve more than half of the term before it is considered a full term.

q: The regular meeting day and the annual meeting should be fixed in the contents of Article V: Meetings in the bylaws.
Article VI of the bylaws deals with the Executive Board (Board of Directors) and should include only their powers.
exp: Article VI of the bylaws deals with the Executive Board (Board of Directors) and should include their powers, how often itis to meet, and ts composition.

q: Article Vil: Committees should provide all the names of the special committees.
exp: Article Vil: mittees should provide all the names of the standing committees, how they are selected, and their composition and duties.

q: A Program Committee, Finance Committee, and a Membership Committee are typical examples of standing committees sted in bylaws.

If Article VII provides that the president "shall be an ex-officio member of all committees except the Nominating Committee," this means that the president may still debate at these committee meetings.
Article Vili: Parliamentary Authority in the bylaws refers to naming a person to serve as the parliamentary authority for the Society.
exp: Article Vill: Parliamentary Authority in the bylaws refers to naming a specific manual of parliamentary practice to govern the Society.

q: If Robert's Rules of Order Newly Revised is adopted as a society's parliamentary authority and another manual is in conflict with a specific point, Robert's Rules of Order Newly Revised is binding.
If the bylaws contain no provision for amending them, they can be amended by a two-thirds vote at any business meeting.
exp: If the bylaws contain no provision for amending them, they can be amended by a two-thirds vote after notice at any business meeting.

q: The articles of bylaws are divided into segments.
exp: The articles of bylaws are divided into sections.

q: If the meaning of a bylaw is not clear, it can be changed by the chair at a special meeting of the officers.
exp: If the meaning of a bylaw is not clear, it can be changed by members through an amendment of the bylaws.

q: The motion to amend the bylaws is a privileged motion.
exp: The motion to amend the bylaws is a main motion.

q: A motion to amend the bylaws should require at least a notice and a two-thirds vote.
A motion to amend the bylaws can be reconsidered if it is an affirmative vote.
exp: A motion to amend the bylaws cannot be reconsidered if it is an affirmative vote.

q: A revision of bylaws can be perfected by third degree amendments.
exp: A revision of bylaws can be perfected by first and second degree amendments. Third degree amendments are never aliowed.

q: When bylaw amendments conflict with one another, the vote is first taken on the amendment which would be least nclusive.
Unless it is nearly unanimous, the final vote on a bylaw amendment should be counted and recorded in the minutes.
Amendments to proposed bylaw amendments may not be made to increase the modification of the article or rule to be amended.
Notice of a bylaw amendment may be worded informally and if it is required to be written, it should be signed by the president and secretary.
exp: Notice of a bylaw amendment should be formally worded and if it is required to be written, it should be signed by the mover and seconder.

q: During a meeting, a member can give notice of a bylaw amendment only during new business.
exp: During a meeting, a member can give notice of a bylaw amendment during new business, the interval between new and unfinished business, or the time after adjournment before the chair has declared the meeting adjourned.

q: If previous notice is given for a bylaw amendment, it will be a general order at the meeting at which it will be considered.
The time at which a bylaw amendment goes into effect is immediately upon adjournment of the meeting.
exp: Generally, the time at which a bylaw amendment goes into effect is immediately upon its adoption.

q: While an amendment to a bylaw is pending, a motion can be made to amend it which requires a majority vote.
The adoption by a society of a proviso to a bylaw amendment requires only a majority vote of the members present and voting.
If there is no change in the meaning of the bylaws, corrections of articles, section numbers, or cross-references can be delegated to the secretary or to a committee.
Members of a society who are chosen especially for a convention as representatives within a larger group of people are called representatives.
exp: Members of a society who are chosen especially for a convention as representatives within a larger group of people are called delegates.

q: Delegates to a convention that consists of several meetings are usually chosen to represent their constituent units for one meeting.
exp: Delegates to a convention that consists of several meetings are usually chosen to represent their constituent units for one session.

q: The term house of delegates or house of representatives applies to delegates who are elected for a fixed term during which they hold sessions from time to time.
In an established state, regional, or national society, the bylaws of the parent body should authorize a periodic convention.
In an established state, regional, or national society composed of constituent parts, delegate qualifications should be prescribed by individual units in their bylaws.
exp: In an established state, regional, or national society composed of constituent parts, delegate qualifications should be prescribed by the bylaws of the parent organization.

q: The bylaws of the parent body of a convention should prescribe the basis for determining the numbers, the ualifications, and the method of electing its delegates and alternates.
Newly elected officers should assume their duties at the beginning of the next convention.
exp: Newly elected officers should assume their duties at the close of the convention.

q: The president of a state unit who is unable to attend the national convention of an established society is replaced by the unit's secretary.
exp: The president of a state unit who is unable to attend the national convention of an established society is replaced by the unit's vice-president.

q: Alternate delegates at a convention are usually seated in a group with the registered delegates.
exp: Alternate delegates at a convention are usually seated apart from registered delegates.

q: In order for an alternate delegate to take the place of an elected delegate who has withdrawn, the alternate must register with the secretary of the society.
exp: In order for an altemate delegate to take the place of an elected delegate who has withdrawn, the altemate must register with the Credentials Committee.

q: A delegate at a convention found out that she must miss the next business meeting. She asked her alternate to take her place. This is not proper unless the rules of the organization provide for it.
When a group of delegates meets during a convention to decide how they will act on certain matters that will come before the convention, it is called an ad hoc meeting.
exp: When a group of delegates meets during a convention to decide how they will act on certain matters that will come before the convention, t is called a caucus.

q: A caucus functions under procedural rules for a committee unless it is large.
A delegate who is under instruction, is required to vote as instructed.
The term caucus is sometimes applied to a standing committee that will support an issue to be brought up.
exp: The term caucus is sometimes applied to a strategy meeting of members of a convention who are avowed supporters of an issue.

q: The Credentials Committee of a convention prepares and certifies the list of altemates, delegates, and officers to the convention.
section: 59. Organization Of A Convention Of An Established Society

q: The Membership and Officer Committees should be most directly involved with the formal organization of a convention.
section: 59. Organization Of A Convention Of An Established Society
exp: The Credentials, Standing Rules, and Program Committees should be most directly involved with the formal organization of a convention.

q: The Program Committee screens and recommends action on original main motions at a convention.
section: 59. Organization Of A Convention Of An Established Society
exp: The Resolutions Committee screens and recommends action on original main motions at a convention.

q: The most important work of a parliamentarian at a convention is rising and calling members of the assembly to order on matters dealing with parliamentary procedure.
section: 59. Organization Of A Convention Of An Established Society
exp: The most important work of a parliamentarian at a convention may be consulting before the convention opens.

q: A convention must officially form itself into a single voting body before it can transact any business.
section: 59. Organization Of A Convention Of An Established Society

q: The first report to be considered at a convention is from the Program Committee.
section: 59. Organization Of A Convention Of An Established Society
exp: The first report to be considered at a convention is from the Credentials Committee.

q: Aconvention cannot be properly organized until the reports of three committees have been considered and adopted. These are, and must be processed in the following order: Credentials, Standing Rules, and Program Committees.
section: 59. Organization Of A Convention Of An Established Society

q: One of the duties of the convention's Credentials Committee is to send each constituent body information about the authorized number of representatives and alternates and their eligibility requirements.
section: 59. Organization Of A Convention Of An Established Society

q: Assume the convention Credentials Committee has received the credentials card from a chapter listing a delegate who s ineligible to serve because of nonpayment of dues. The Credentials Committee should advise the chapter that it has the right to choose another alternate.
section: 59. Organization Of A Convention Of An Established Society

q: One of the responsibilities of the Credentials Committee is to draft standing rules for a convention.
section: 59. Organization Of A Convention Of An Established Society
exp: One of the responsibilities of the Credentials Committee is to make ements for registration to take place at a convention.

q: Two responsibilities of the Credentials Committee are to record members as they are officially registered and to verify that members' credentials are correct.
section: 59. Organization Of A Convention Of An Established Society

q: In a convention lasting several days, it is recommended that registration begin the same day the convention opens.
section: 59. Organization Of A Convention Of An Established Society
exp: Ina convention lasting several days, it is recommended that registration begin one or two days before the convention begins.

q: The motion to Recess is not in order before the receipt of the Credentials Committee report at a convention.
section: 59. Organization Of A Convention Of An Established Society
exp: The motion to Recess is in order before the receipt of the Credentials Committee report at a convention.

q: After the Credentials Committee report is presented at a convention, the next step is for the chair to ask for unanimous consent approval of the report.
section: 59. Organization Of A Convention Of An Established Society
exp: After the Credentials Committee report is presented at a convention, the next step normally is for the chair to ask if there are questions on the report.

q: When the report of the Credentials Committee is adopted, it is then the official roll of voting members of the convention.
section: 59. Organization Of A Convention Of An Established Society

q: lf several voting members register after the Credentials Committee has made its report and their status is not uestioned, they still may not participate.
section: 59. Organization Of A Convention Of An Established Society
exp: If several voting members register after the Credentials Committee has made its report and their status is not questioned, they may participate.

q: If the bylaws of the convention's standing rules do not prescribe a quorum, the quorum is a majority of the registered delegates who have not departed.
section: 59. Organization Of A Convention Of An Established Society
exp: If the bylaws of the convention's standing rules do not prescribe a quorum, the quorum is a majority of the registered delegates irrespective of any who have departed.

q: Standing rules of a convention contain "parliamentary" rules related to the conduct of business and nonparliamentary rules.
section: 59. Organization Of A Convention Of An Established Society

q: A group of rules known as "The Standing Rules of the Convention" apply to future conventions.
section: 59. Organization Of A Convention Of An Established Society
exp: A group of rules known as "The Standing Rules of the Convention" apply to that one convention only.
