q: Formal disciplinary procedures should be regarded as a drastic step used for serious situations.
The maximum penaity that an organization can inflict on a member is a suspension.
exp: The extreme penalty that an organization can impose on a member is an expulsion.

q: Nonmembers can be excluded at any time from part or all of a meeting by a question of privilege and a motion to "go nto executive session."
Ali persons in attendance at a meeting have an obligation to follow the legitimate orders of the presiding officer.
The presiding officer should never use the gavel to drown out a disorderly member.
If you were chair and a member's debate was not germane, you should loudly cail the member out of order and ollow with a reprimand.
exp: If you were chair and a member's debate was not germane, you should rap the gavel ligh' int out the fault, and advise the member to stay on the pending topic.

q: A member who wishes to call another member out of order must rise, address the chair, and wait to be recognized.
exp: A member who wishes to call another member out of order need not gain recognition from the chair.

q: Assume the chair "names" a member for a breach of order. This means the member has committed a serious breach of order, the chair is preferring charges, and the assembly may impose a penalty.
If there is an offense against the assembly during a meeting such as a member using objectional words, there is no need for a formal trial with witnesses.
A member who uses objectionable or disorderly words in a meeting can be removed by a vote of the assembly.
It takes two members to require the vote on the imposition of a penalty to be taken by ballot.
exp: A single member can require the vote on the imposition of a penalty to be taken by ballot.

q: During the proceedings of a meeting, the chair may grant nonmembers attending rights such as voting and debating.
exp: During the proceedings of a meeting, nonmembers that are attending have no rights.

q: Nonmembers who are an annoyance at a meeting can be removed from the meeting by an order from the sergeant-at- arms.
exp: Nonmembers who are an annoyance at a meeting can be removed by an order from the chair.

q: A formal trial of a member of a society who has been accused of injuring the name of the organization must be held n a special meeting.
exp: A formal trial of a member of a society who has been accused of injuring the name of the organization must be held in executive session.

q: The society has the right to let anyone know the reason why an expelled member of the society has been found guilty.
exp: The society does not have the right to let anyone know the reason why an expelled member of the society has been found guilty. 122

q: A trial by a society can only establish the guilt of the accused regarding fitness for membership in the society. }
The first step in a fair disciplinary process should be a formal notification to the public that a member is accused.
exp: The first step in a fair disciplinary process should be a confidential investigation by a committee.

q: If a member of a society is suspected of improper conduct against the society, there should be a confidential nvestigation by a standing committee of the society.
exp: !f a member of a society is suspected of improper conduct against the society, there should be a confidential investigation by a select (or special) committee of the society.

q: A member accused of serious misconduct is entitled to due process before any penalty can be imposed. An nvestigation by an outsider such as an auditor, police, or private detective is not proper in the procedure.
If an organization's bylaws do not include a method of charge and trial, a member should offer a resolution to appoint an investigating committee.
An appointed investigative committee does not have the power to require the accused to appear before it.
At a disciplinary trial, the "managers" present the case against the accused, in effect acting as prosecutors.
If a trial is ordered before a committee or a regular assembly, the secretary is only obligated to send to the accused the notification of the date, place, and hour of the trial.
exp: Ifa trial is ordered before a committee or a regular assembly, the secretary is obligated to send to the accused notification of the date, place, and hour of the trial, the charge (s), and the fact that the accused is directed to appear as cited.

q: During the trial procedure, the accused is not allowed to call witnesses.
exp: During the trial procedure, the accused is allowed to call witnesses.

q: Nonmembers who are witnesses at a trial should be in the room during the entire trial.
exp: Nonmembers who are witnesses at a trial should be in the room only while testifying.

q: If the accused at a trial fails to appear at the appointed time as directed, the trial is canceled.
exp: If the accused at a trial fails to appear at the appointed time as directed, the trial proceeds without the accused.

q: If you were chair at a trial, your first action would be to remind the assembly that the meeting is in executive session and that all business must be kept secret.
After the preliminaries are taken in a trial of a member, the chair directs the secretary to read the charges.
The second step in the procedure of a trial is opening statements by both sides.
exp: The second step in the procedure of a trial is for the chair to ask the accused how he/she pleads--guilty or not guilty.

q: The third step in a trial if the plea is not guilty is the testimony of witnesses.
exp: The third step in a trial if the plea is not guilty is the opening statements.

q: After the closing arguments of a trial are completed, each charge is opened for debate and voted on separately.
If the accused is found guilty at a trial, a motion can be made for expulsion, which requires a minimum affirmative vote of a majority.
exp: If the accused is found guilty at a trial, a motion can be made for expulsion, which requires a minimum affirmative vote of two-thirds.

q: If a trial is held before a committee instead of the assembly of a society, the assembly votes (in executive session) on the resolutions submitted by the committee.
Some professional societies have a standing committee on discipline, and one prescribed duty of this committee is to mpose a penalty.
exp: Some professional societies have a standing committee on discipline, and some prescribed duties of this committee are to manage a trial or the society, to investigate disciplinary problems, and to hear a trial. The committee should not be empowered to impose a penalty.

q: A member can raise a Point of Order if a motion is made and seconded and the chair ignores it.
If a member is ignored on a Point of Order that was called because the presiding officer refused to put a motion, the maker of the motion can put the motion to a vote.
The regular presiding officer who does not properly perform the duties of the chair at a meeting, can be censured.

If the chair is occupied by a member who is not the regular presiding officer, and the assembly feels that the member should vacate the chair, the assembly can propose a motion to "declare the chair vacant and proceed to elect a new chair."

If the bylaws state that officers shall serve "for four years or until their successors are elected," a motion can be adopted to reconsider the election if an elected officer should be deposed from office for misconduct.
exp: If the bylaws state that officers shall serve "for four years or until their successors are elected," the election of the officer can be rescinded an elected officer should be deposed from office for misconduct.
